* notebook: add veronica-core circuit breaker integration example

Adds tools_veronica_circuit_breaker.ipynb demonstrating how to protect
AG2 agents with CircuitBreakerCapability from the veronica-core library.

Three self-contained demos:
- Demo 1: Basic circuit breaker (opens after N consecutive None replies)

fix: correct token-to-char budget calculation in TokenLimiter (#2577)

The TokenLimiter was using `max_tokens // chars_per_token` to convert
a token budget into a character budget, but the correct formula is
`max_tokens * chars_per_token`. For example, with max_tokens=10000 and
chars_per_token=4 (default), the old code computed a 2500-char budget
instead of the correct 40000-char budget, causing the middleware to
aggressively over-trim message history when using the default
chars_per_token value.

The bug was masked in tests because all test cases used chars_per_token=1,
where division and multiplication produce the same result.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: correct duplicate condition in speaker selection verbose logging (#2578)

The `elif` branch on line 889 had `no_of_mentions == 1`, duplicating the
`if` condition on line 879.  This made the elif dead code and caused
`SpeakerAttemptFailedMultipleAgentsEvent` to never fire — when multiple
agents were mentioned, execution fell through to the `else` branch and
incorrectly emitted `SpeakerAttemptFailedNoAgentsEvent`.

Changed the condition to `no_of_mentions > 1` so the three branches now
correctly cover: exactly one mention (success), more than one (failed,
multiple agents), and zero (failed, no agents).

* feat: AgentEligibilityPolicy for runtime GroupChat candidate filtering

Add AgentEligibilityPolicy Protocol to GroupChat, enabling runtime
filtering of speaker candidates based on agent health or business logic.

- AgentEligibilityPolicy: runtime_checkable Protocol with is_eligible()
- SelectionContext: frozen dataclass (round, last_speaker, participants)
- AgentDescriptionGuard: prepends [UNAVAILABLE] to steer LLM selection
- GroupChat.eligibility_policies field (default [], no breaking changes)
- _apply_eligibility_policies() called inside _prepare_and_select_agents
- AND semantics: all policies must pass for agent to be eligible
- Callable speaker_selection_method bypasses policies (explicit control)

Addresses speaker-selection gap identified by @marklysze in #2430:
when an agent fails, GroupChat can now exclude it from future rounds.

* style: apply ruff formatter fixes

Slice spacing and line-wrapping adjustments from pre-commit.

* fix: pass filtered agents to manual fallback in select_speaker

Manual mode fallback (next_agent) was using the full agent roster,
bypassing eligibility policy filtering. Now passes the
policy-filtered candidate list to next_agent in both sync and
async paths.

* test: cover func_call_filter fallback path with eligibility policies

Adds two tests for the fallback code path where no agent can execute
the requested function and GroupChat falls back to all agents with
function_map:
- Happy path: policy filters one agent, remaining agent selected
- Adversarial: policy blocks all function_map agents, raises
  NoEligibleSpeakerError

* test: cover async manual fallback path in a_select_speaker

Adds test for the async manual mode fallback (L678) where
manual_select_speaker returns None and a_select_speaker falls back to
next_agent with policy-filtered agents. Also removes unused variable
flagged by ruff.

* test: improve coverage with rule-based audit (+5 tests, -2 bloat)

Add sync manual fallback, AND-invariant, compound state (policy +
allow_repeat_speaker=False), boundary triple, and string parse
robustness tests. Remove 2 duplicate/tautological tests.

50 -> 54 tests, all passing.

* style: fix ruff formatter parametrize indentation

* test: add double-prefix guard and None description noop test

- Assert description.count("[UNAVAILABLE]") <= 1 in toggle thread test
- Add test_mark_available_noop_on_none_description (never marked unavailable)

* fix: harden eligibility policy edge cases

- Guard empty candidates after transition filtering when policies were
  already applied (prevent silent fallback to all agents)
- Use _UNSET sentinel in AgentDescriptionGuard to distinguish "never
  marked" from "original was None" (prevents unexpected None restoration)
- Clear stale guard state on mark_available early-return path
- Add regression tests for empty-candidates and description guard edges

* style: fix ruff format on _no_transition_constraints

* test: add coverage for str-participants rejection and external prefix strip

- test_selection_context_rejects_str_participants: bare str raises TypeError
- test_mark_available_strips_external_prefix: guard strips prefix added by

PR #2713 refactored ``ToolResult`` from a single-valued ``content`` field to a
list of ``parts`` (``TextInput``/``DataInput``/``BinaryInput``/``UrlInput``/
``FileIdInput``) so tools can return multi-part, multi-modal results. Every
consumer of the old API was updated except the AG-UI adapter: ``autogen/beta/
ag_ui/stream.py`` still reads ``event.content`` on ``ToolResultEvent``.

``ToolResultEvent`` no longer has a ``content`` attribute, so every run that
invokes any tool crashes with:

    AttributeError: 'ToolResultEvent' object has no attribute 'content'

…right after the ``TOOL_CALL_ARGS`` SSE frame and before any ``TOOL_CALL_RESULT``
reaches the browser. This happens on every provider — the bug is downstream of
the LLM client.

Fix: introduce ``_stringify_tool_result`` that flattens ``ToolResult.parts``
into the plain ``str`` that AG-UI's wire format expects. Text passes through;
structured data is JSON-encoded via ``to_jsonable_python``; URLs/file-ids/
binaries get compact, human-readable placeholders; multiple parts are joined
with newlines.

Adds a new ``test/beta/ag_ui/`` suite (there were none) with unit coverage for
the helper and an end-to-end case that drives a scripted agent through
``AGUIStream.dispatch`` and asserts ``TOOL_CALL_RESULT.content`` is both
present and correctly serialised for string and dict tool returns.

* fix(beta/anthropic): dedupe tool_result blocks when wrapper + individual events both present

Tool completions produce two events in order: an individual
ToolResultEvent (emitted by the tool itself, awaited by _execute_call)
and a ToolResultsEvent wrapper (emitted by execute_tools after
gathering). The Anthropic history→messages mapper processed both
branches in event_list order: the individual branch emitted first
and added to emitted_result_ids, but the wrapper branch never checked
the set, so it emitted the same tool_use_id again. Anthropic 400'd
on the duplicate tool_result blocks.

Pre-scan event_list for ToolResultsEvent wrappers and seed
emitted_result_ids with their parent_ids before the main loop. The
individual-fallback branch's existing `parent not in emitted_result_ids`
check now correctly skips when a wrapper is present; when no wrapper
exists, the fallback still fires as before.

Likely mirrored in other provider mappers — this patch covers
Anthropic only.

feat(beta): add Task lifecycle primitive (#2774)

* feat(beta): add Task lifecycle primitive

A Task is a wrapper any Agent can use to give a unit of work a
trackable lifecycle. The Task emits TaskStarted, TaskProgress,
TaskCompleted, TaskFailed, and TaskExpired events on a bound stream
so observers (UI, watchers, test harnesses) can follow along without
participating in execution.

Tasks are agent-owned. The framework does not assign or schedule
them. Standalone usage requires no observers — events fly past
harmlessly if no observer subscribes.

Public surface:
- autogen.beta.Task — the lifecycle handle
- autogen.beta.TaskSpec — what the task is doing (title, description,
  payload, optional capability tag)
- autogen.beta.TaskState — CREATED, RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED, EXPIRED
- autogen.beta.TaskMetadata — mutable lifecycle record
- autogen.beta.TaskInject — Annotated injection for the active task,
  resolved by fast_depends inside an `async with agent.task(...):` block
- Agent.task(...) — context-manager entry point
- Agent.add_policy(...) — public assembly-policy registration

Event additions:
- TaskExpired event (new) emitted when a task TTL elapses
- TaskCompleted.result widened to Any
- TaskStarted gains optional spec field
- TaskProgress gains optional payload field

Ship the entire network module except the LLM-facing tool surface.
After this commit, agents can register through a hub, exchange
envelopes inside protocol-defined sessions (consulting / conversation
/ discussion / workflow), participate in turn-taking via the default
notify handler, and observe each other's tasks — all by writing
tenant code that calls the public APIs directly. The six LLM-facing
tools (say / delegate / peers / sessions / tasks / context) and
NetworkPlugin land in a follow-up.

What ships
----------
Identity & protocol data:
- Passport (immutable id + billing) + Resume (mutable claims +
  observed track record) + AgentRuntime
- AuthAdapter / NoAuth registry
- Envelope + stable event-type constants
- SessionManifest / Expectation / Participant / SessionMetadata
- Rule (access + limits, including delegation depth + concurrency caps)
- Transition vocabulary (TransitionGraph + 5 targets + 3 conditions)
- TaskMirror (bridges agent Task* events to Hub.observe_task)

Transport:
- LinkClient / LinkEndpoint Protocols + frame vocabulary
- LocalLink (in-process duplex)

Session adapters:
- SessionAdapter Protocol + AdapterState marker + AdapterResult
- ConsultingAdapter (1Q1R), ConversationAdapter (1+1 bidirectional),
  DiscussionAdapter (round_robin), WorkflowAdapter (transition-driven)

View policies:
- ViewPolicy Protocol
- FullTranscript + WindowedSummary (bounded prompt size at any turn count)

Hub:
- Registry (passport / resume / rule / skill + name and capability
  indexes), per-session WAL + adapter state cache, dispatch, audit
  log, TTL sweeper, expectation sweeper (acks_within / reply_within
  / max_silence × audit / notify_session / auto_close)

Tenant-side client:
- NetworkClient Protocol + HubClient + AgentClient
- Session / ClientTask handles
- Default notify handler (auto-acks invites; runs Agent.ask on
  EV_TEXT and EV_HANDOFF; routes through the configured ViewPolicy)
- Dependency-injection annotations + skill-render helpers

* fix(sliding_window): drop orphan tool results

window. A ToolResultsEvent whose matching ToolCallsEvent was trimmed but that
survived deeper in the window (mid-window orphan, or events carried over
between agents on shared streams) passed through and caused providers (OpenAI)

    to a preceeding message with 'tool_calls'.

are dropped. Add tests for mid-window orphans, multi-position orphans, and
the paired-and-kept case.

Fixes #2793

TokenBudgetPolicy carried the same head-only orphan-stripping logic as
SlidingWindowPolicy and shared the same bug: orphan ToolResultsEvents at
non-leading positions in the budgeted window survived and triggered
provider 400s.

orphan test to mirror the sliding_window coverage.

feat(beta/network): HumanClient + observability foundation (#2801)

* feat(beta/network): add HumanClient + Passport.kind for native HITL

A non-LLM participant in the network. Implements the NetworkClient Protocol
directly — no Agent, no plugin, no assembly policies. External code drives
it through two surfaces:

  - push: on_envelope(callback) fires per inbound envelope
  - pull: next_envelope(predicate, timeout) / envelopes() async iterator

Outbound sends use the same primitives as AgentClient (send / open /
post_envelope). open() returns a Channel handle compatible with the
AgentClient-shaped pattern so a UI can drive multi-turn channels without
adapter-specific code. Auto-acks channel invites by default so the hub-side
quorum handshake completes without UI round-trips; embedders pass
auto_ack_invites=False to gate joins manually.

Passport.kind: Literal["agent", "human", "remote_agent"] | None discriminates
participant types. None is the back-compat alias for "agent". "remote_agent"
is reserved for a future federation / A2A bridge. Hub.list_agents accepts a
kind= filter so discovery tools can scope by participant type.

HubClient gains register_human(passport, *, resume=None, rule=None,
auto_ack_invites=True). register() now rejects kind="human" with a guidance
error pointing at register_human so the two paths stay obvious.

by sending the initial question; the graph's FromSpeaker(user) →
AgentTarget(triage) advances the turn naturally instead of via a direct
agent.ask hack that bypassed the network.

Adds 13 unit tests covering register, push + pull, callback exception
isolation, consulting where the human is the respondent, human-initiated
consulting against an agent, round-robin discussion with a human gating on
adapter state for its turn, chunk no-op, post-disconnect raise, and
list_agents kind filter.

State-transition observability and a swappable decision-making seam

HubListener — read-only Protocol the hub fan-outs to after every
state change: on_envelope_posted / on_envelope_rejected /
on_dispatch_failed / on_channel_event / on_agent_event /
on_expectation_fired / on_turn_failed / on_task_event /
on_inbox_pressure. BaseHubListener is the no-op base so users

fix(fast_depends): route keyword-passed positional_or_keyword params before **kwargs (#1790) (#2813)

`CallModel._solve` only popped declared keyword-only parameters from the
incoming kwargs dict before assigning the leftover into the function's
`**var_keyword_arg` slot. POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD params (the common case
for a normally-typed function argument like `arg1: str`) never reach
their own slot when the caller passes them by name — they leak into the
catch-all and the wrapped function sees them as missing.

This is the path tools register-for-llm goes through, so any user tool
declaring both regular args and `**kwargs` (with annotations) fails when
the LLM sends arguments back as JSON. Reproduction in #1790.

Pop POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD params from kwargs first, then fill
`**var_keyword_arg` with what's actually left over. Behavior is
unchanged for functions without a `**kwargs` catch-all.

Adds three regression tests in test/fast_depends/sync/test_cast.py
covering the broken case, the kwargs-only case, and the positional-call
case.

fix(beta/filesystem): pin read/write encoding to UTF-8 (#2818)

* fix(beta/filesystem): pin read/write encoding to UTF-8

The FilesystemToolkit's read_file, write_file, and update_file helpers
called Path.read_text() / Path.write_text() without an explicit
encoding. Both default to locale.getpreferredencoding(), which is
'cp1252' on most Windows installs and raises:

- UnicodeDecodeError on read for any file whose bytes are not valid
  cp1252 (most modern source files, JSON/YAML with non-ASCII strings,
  Markdown with smart quotes, anything with emoji or CJK glyphs).
- UnicodeEncodeError on write for any payload the model generates that
  is not representable in cp1252 (the same set of characters).

Update file then reads with the platform default and writes with the
platform default in the same call, so a round-trip on Windows silently
transcodes the file every time the model edits it.

Pass encoding='utf-8' to all three call sites so the toolkit produces
the same bytes on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

Adds three regression tests that drive the toolkit through Agent.ask
and assert byte-level equality against the UTF-8 encoding of the
payload:

- test_write_file_encodes_as_utf8 pins write_file
- test_read_file_decodes_as_utf8 pins read_file
- test_update_file_preserves_utf8 pins the read+write pair in
  update_file (with a non-cp1252 replacement string)

Existing locale-default reads in older tests (test_write_file,
test_update_file) keep their assertions; they pass on POSIX where the
default is already UTF-8 and the new tests pin the contract on every
platform.

PythonEnvironment._write_to_file is the shared helper every concrete

* fix(interop/langchain): use arun for async langchain tools

LangChainInteroperability.convert_tool always wrapped the langchain tool with
the sync run() dispatcher, even when the tool defined a native async
implementation. Inside an asyncio event loop (e.g. a_initiate_chat), this
blocks on the synchronous path and degrades concurrency.

`coroutine=...` or BaseTool subclasses that override `_arun` — and wrap
those with an async function that awaits `langchain_tool.arun(...)`. Sync
tools keep the existing sync wrapper for backward compatibility, and the
behavior for tools whose async impl is just a thread-pool fallback of
`_run` is left unchanged.

class-based BaseTool subclasses with overridden _arun.

fix: write generated text artifacts as UTF-8 to avoid Windows charmap errors (#2815)

Seven `open(path, "w")` / `Path.open("w")` sites across the codebase
rely on the platform's `locale.getpreferredencoding()`. On Windows
that is typically `cp1252`, so writing any text containing characters
outside Latin-1 — Unicode in agent names / descriptions, generated
Python source with `é` / `中文` / emoji literals, JSON saved from
LLM-produced configs, Jupyter HTML cell outputs with math glyphs,
etc. — crashes with:

    UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character ...

This is the same bug class reported in #1731 (DocAgent PDF ingest)
and #1167 (older `'ascii' codec` variant). #1731 is fixed in a
companion PR for `parser_utils.py`; this PR cleans up the remaining
matching paths so a Windows user does not hit the next instance of
the same bug after upgrading.

Sites covered, all switched to `encoding="utf-8"`:

* `autogen/agentchat/contrib/captainagent/agent_builder.py`
  — `save_config_*.json` builder cache.
* `autogen/agentchat/contrib/captainagent/captainagent.py`
  — `build_history_*.json` persistence.
* `autogen/coding/jupyter/embedded_ipython_code_executor.py`
  — HTML output dump from notebook cells.
* `autogen/coding/jupyter/jupyter_code_executor.py`
  — same HTML dump on the non-embedded executor.
* `autogen/mcp/mcp_proxy/mcp_proxy.py`
  — generated `main.py` and rendered config files.
* `autogen/tools/experimental/google/authentication/credentials_local_provider.py`
  — Google OAuth `token.json` cache (already UTF-8 per Google spec).

JSON is UTF-8 by RFC 8259, Python source is UTF-8 by PEP 3120,
generated HTML defaults to UTF-8, and the Google token file is
UTF-8 by the OAuth client library's own format. The previous code
just relied on the platform default lining up with that, which
isn't true on Windows.

No behaviour change on Linux / macOS.

fix(document_agent): write Docling conversion artifacts as UTF-8 (#1731) (#2814)

* fix(document_agent): write Docling conversion artifacts as UTF-8 (#1731)

`docling_convert_and_save` opens three output files (markdown / json /
html table) using the default `Path.open("w")`, which inherits the
platform's `locale.getpreferredencoding()`. On Windows that is
typically `cp1252`, so any document character outside Latin-1 — common
Unicode glyphs like `U+2612` (ballot box with X), `U+2264` (less-than-
or-equal-to), and similar symbols that appear in real PDFs — crashes
Docling ingestion with:

    'charmap' codec can't encode character '☒' in position N:
    character maps to <undefined>

This is the exact failure shape reported in #1731, and the same class
of bug as #1167 (the older `'ascii' codec` variant).

Add `encoding="utf-8"` to each `output_file.open("w")` call in
`autogen/agents/experimental/document_agent/parser_utils.py`. The
markdown and JSON artifacts are both specified to be UTF-8 anyway
(JSON by RFC 8259, markdown by docling), so the previous reliance on
the platform default was always incorrect; this just makes it
explicit and portable.

No behaviour change on Linux / macOS, where the default already
resolves to UTF-8.

Closes #1731.

Adds two complementary tests so the codecov delta on this PR is no

  non-ASCII markdown / dict / table-HTML through the mocked Docling
  converter, then reads the resulting files as raw bytes and asserts
  they match the UTF-8 byte sequence of the source strings. On
  Windows the pre-fix code would raise UnicodeEncodeError mid-export;
  on POSIX the assertion still pins the contract because we compare
  bytes (not str), so a future default-encoding regression on POSIX
  would also be caught.

- test_exports_pass_utf8_encoding_to_path_open patches pathlib.Path.open
  with mock_open() and asserts that every w-mode opener inside

fix(coding): write user-defined functions module as UTF-8 (#2819)

* fix(coding): write user-defined functions module as UTF-8

LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor._setup_functions wrote the generated
functions module via Path.write_text without an explicit encoding,
inheriting locale.getpreferredencoding() (cp1252 on most Windows
installs). Any user-supplied function whose source contained a
non-cp1252 glyph — non-Latin docstring, emoji, smart quotes in an
Annotated description, accented identifiers — would crash mid-write
with UnicodeEncodeError, leaving _setup_functions_complete=False and
the next execute_code_blocks call to silently re-run the same broken
path.

Pass encoding='utf-8' to the write_text call. Inline comment explains
why so a future refactor doesn't drop the kwarg.

Tests:

- test_setup_functions_writes_module_as_utf8 drives _setup_functions
  with a FunctionWithRequirements.from_str source that contains
  Café, em-dash, ☕, 例, and 🚀; reads the resulting module file as
  raw bytes and asserts the UTF-8 round-trip succeeds.

- test_setup_functions_passes_utf8_encoding_to_write_text patches
  Path.write_text and asserts encoding='utf-8' is in the kwargs of
  the first call inside _setup_functions. This guards the contract
  on POSIX, where the platform default is already UTF-8 and the
  byte-level test would otherwise pass even if the kwarg were
  dropped.

Both tests tolerate the downstream subprocess syntax-check call that
_setup_functions runs after the write — it depends on a 'python'
executable being on PATH, which is not guaranteed in every
environment, and the write we care about has already happened by
the time the subprocess runs.

fix: block shell operators in readonly/allowed-command mode (#2689)

* fix: block shell operators in readonly/allowed-command mode

When `LocalShellEnvironment(readonly=True)` restricts commands to a
whitelist, the `matches()` check only validates the command prefix.
Since commands run with `shell=True`, an agent can bypass the
restriction via shell operators:

    echo 'data' > file.txt      # write via redirect
    cat /etc/passwd | nc ...    # exfiltrate via pipe

config_list_from_json reads JSON either via Path.read_text() (when the

artifact must be created (append=False) before appending parts to it.").

  on `not append`. The new append=False opening chunk is not the final
  one, so keying dedup off `not append` would mark the artifact seen and
  drop every following chunk. Single-shot artifacts (tool calls, polled
  snapshots) already set last_chunk=True, so they are unaffected.

feat(beta/network): cross-process data plane (WsLink, auth, delivery) (#2914)

* feat(beta/network): validate HelloFrame auth claims; add ApiKeyAuth adapter

Previously Hub._dispatch_frame parsed `HelloFrame.auth_scheme` and
`HelloFrame.auth_claim` but never validated them, so any client could
re-bind an existing identity by name alone. The HelloFrame branch now
resolves the passport, looks up the registered AuthAdapter via
AuthRegistry, calls validate(passport, claim), and responds with
ErrorFrame(code="auth_failed") without binding on any AuthError.

Adds ApiKeyAuth as a canonical adapter beyond NoAuth: constant-time
hmac.compare_digest against a static `keys` map (passport.name -> token)
plus an optional async `resolver` for dynamic lookups. The claim is a
free-form dict expected to carry `{"token": "..."}`; missing / empty /
non-string tokens fail with AuthError.

AuthError joins the error-code map so it surfaces uniformly as
"auth_failed" wherever Hub frame-handlers convert exceptions.

* feat(beta/network): at-least-once delivery via inbox cursor + causation dedup

Wires receipts, replay, and idempotency into the hub so dispatch is
durable across reconnects and reorderings.

* HelloFrame gains optional ``since_envelope_id``; ReceiptFrame gains
  ``recipient_id`` so a single endpoint hosting multiple agents can
  ack on the right cursor.
* Hub tracks ``_inbox_cursors`` (agent_id -> last acked envelope_id),
  persisted at ``agents/{id}/inbox.cursor``. Cursor advance is
  monotonic — out-of-order acks do not rewind. NACKs are logged but
  leave the cursor in place so the next reconnect replays.
* Hub tracks ``_causation_index`` ((channel_id, sender_id,
  causation_id) -> envelope_id) populated on every WAL append,
  pruned when a channel transitions to a terminal state, and
  rebuilt from active-channel WALs on hydrate. Public async
  ``Hub.find_envelope_by_causation`` resolves a key back to its
  accepted envelope so handlers can short-circuit duplicate work.
* HelloFrame reconnect with ``since_envelope_id`` walks each active
  channel the agent participates in and re-emits unacked NotifyFrames
  past ``max(cursor, since_envelope_id)``, skipping the agent's own
  sends and envelopes not addressed to them.
* ``HubClient._dispatch_notify`` now auto-acks each delivered
  envelope (and NACKs on handler exceptions), so the cursor tracks
  the WAL head under the in-process flow without tenant changes.
* unregister clears the cursor and deletes its disk file.

* feat(beta/network): reconnect-by-name via HubClient.attach + pending turns

Adds the API surface a tenant needs to resume an agent's work after a
process restart: re-bind by name to the existing identity, query what
turns the protocol expects, and re-fire the notify handler against
their triggering envelopes.

* New ChannelAdapter Protocol method `expected_next(metadata, state)
  -> ExpectedTurn | None`. ExpectedTurn carries the expected agent_id
  and the envelope that put the turn on them (so a reconnect can
  recreate the notify input without inventing one). DiscussionAdapter
  and WorkflowAdapter delegate to their folded `expected_next_speaker`
  + `last_envelope_id`; ConsultingAdapter walks the 1Q1R flags;
  ConversationAdapter (free-form) returns None via the new
  `default_expected_next` helper.
* `Hub.pending_turns_for(agent_id) -> list[PendingTurn]` walks every
  active channel the agent participates in, asks the adapter, and
  surfaces a PendingTurn per channel where the agent is named. The
  triggering envelope's `created_at` is read from the WAL.
* `HubClient.attach(agent, name, ...)` reconnect API: re-binds the
  named identity to the new connection's endpoint when it exists,
  otherwise falls back to `register`. The hub-side `bind_endpoint`
  evicts the prior agent->endpoint mapping but keeps the prior
  endpoint alive so other agents bound to it keep working.
* `AgentClient.resume_pending_turns()` queries the hub, fetches each
  trigger envelope from the WAL, and feeds them back through
  `self.receive`. Skips entries with no triggering envelope (e.g. a
  freshly opened channel where the creator has nothing to react to
  yet).

* feat(beta/network): WebSocket transport — WsLink + serve_ws

Carries the existing Frame vocabulary over a real WebSocket so a hub
in one process can serve agents living in another. JSON-encoded
frames flow over the same encode/decode helpers ``LocalLink`` uses,
so any wire-side serialization issue surfaces at the framework
boundary rather than in tenant code.

* ``WsLinkClient`` connects via ``await client.open()`` and exposes
  the LinkClient Protocol (send_frame, frames iterator, close). The
  server-assigned ``endpoint_id`` is observed off the inbound
  ``WelcomeFrame`` and cached on the client.
* ``WsLinkEndpoint`` mirrors the same Protocol on the hub side; one
  instance per active connection. Constructed by ``serve_ws`` and
  attached to the hub via ``Hub.attach_endpoint``.
* ``serve_ws(hub, host, port, *, ssl_context=...)`` is an async
  context manager spawning a ``websockets.asyncio`` server bound to
  the hub. Heartbeat is delegated to ``ping_interval`` / ``ping_timeout``
  on the underlying library — no separate ``PingFrame`` traffic.
* ``Hub._handle_endpoint`` now releases endpoint + agent bindings
  in a ``finally`` block, so a dropped connection no longer leaves
  stale entries in ``_endpoints_by_id`` or ``_agent_to_endpoint``.
* New optional extra ``ag2[network-ws]`` aliases the existing
  ``websockets`` dep. When ``websockets`` is not installed, the
  ``WsLink`` re-exports degrade to a ``missing_optional_dependency``
  stub that raises on first use with a clear install hint.

* feat(beta/network): federation dispatch seam via RemoteAgentProxy

Adds the Protocol surface a tenant uses to dispatch envelopes to
participants that live on another hub. The framework ships zero
proxy implementations — the seam is the deliverable.

* New ``RemoteAgentProxy`` Protocol in ``network/remote.py``:
  ``scheme: str``, async ``dispatch(envelope, recipient)``, async
  ``close()``. Runtime-checkable so callers can detect impls.
* ``Hub.register_remote_proxy(proxy)`` + ``unregister_remote_proxy`` +
  ``remote_proxy_for`` indexed by ``proxy.scheme``.
* ``Hub._dispatch`` routes recipients whose passport has
  ``effective_kind == "remote_agent"`` through the proxy registered
  for ``recipient.auth.scheme`` instead of looking up a local
  endpoint. Missing proxy or proxy exception fires
  ``on_dispatch_failed`` and continues with remaining recipients.
* ``Hub.register`` skips local auth validation for
  ``kind="remote_agent"`` passports — their auth claim is a routing
  label consumed by the proxy, not a credential the local hub can
  validate.
* New ``Passport.hub_id: str | None`` field — None for local
  registrations, set for participants the hub caches as proxies for
  another hub. Round-trips through ``to_dict`` / ``from_dict``.
* New ``parse_hub_urn(s) -> tuple[str | None, str]`` in
  ``network/ids.py``. Splits ``hub://<hub_id>/<agent_id>`` URNs into
  parts; returns ``(None, s)`` for non-URN or malformed inputs so
  callers can use it without branching on shape.

* feat(beta/task): cancellation + opt-in checkpoint/resume

Owner-driven cancellation joins the existing complete/fail/expire
terminal paths, and a small ``CheckpointStore`` Protocol lets owners
persist resume state across restarts. Standalone agents pay no cost
unless they wire a store; networked agents get a hub-backed default.

* New ``TaskState.CANCELLED`` (terminal) + ``TaskCancelled`` event
  carrying a free-form ``reason``. ``Task.cancel(reason)`` is the
  owner-side trigger; idempotent on already-terminal tasks.
* ``CheckpointStore`` Protocol (runtime_checkable) in
  ``autogen.beta.task``: async ``write(task_id, state)`` and async
  ``read(task_id) -> dict | None``. Payloads are opaque — the
  framework never inspects them.
* ``Task.checkpoint(state)`` writes via the configured store; silent
  no-op without a store or when the task is already terminal.
  ``Task(... resume_from=prior_task_id)`` reads the prior snapshot
  into ``task.resumed_state`` so the owner can pick up mid-flow.
  ``Agent.task(...)`` exposes both kwargs.
* ``Hub.checkpoint_task(task_id, state)`` + ``read_task_checkpoint``
  persist a single JSON blob at ``tasks/{task_id}/checkpoint.json``
  (last-write-wins; ``task_checkpoint_path`` is the new layout
  helper). ``HubBackedCheckpointStore`` in
  ``network.client.checkpoint`` is the canonical
  ``CheckpointStore`` impl, delegating to those hub methods so
  network-attached agents get durability without extra setup.

* feat(beta/network): bridge task cancellation; surface public hub accessors

TaskMirror now forwards TaskCancelled events to the hub the same way it
already handles TaskCompleted/Failed/Expired — update_task(state=CANCELLED,
error=reason) plus record_observation for capability-tagged tasks. Without
this bridge, owner-driven Task.cancel() left the hub's TaskMetadata at
RUNNING forever and capability stats never reflected cancellations.

The tasks LLM verb's cancel action stops returning a placeholder and now
posts an ag2.task.cancel_request envelope into the task's channel
addressed to the owner; the owner is free to honour by calling
Task.cancel or to ignore. Two new event-type constants ship:
EV_TASK_CANCEL_REQUEST and EV_TASK_CANCELLED.

Hub.find_agent_id (non-raising) and Hub.get_rule (raises NotFoundError)
become public surface so HubClient.attach can rebuild an AgentClient
from persisted identity through public accessors instead of reaching
into hub privates. HubClient gains matching passthroughs.

Design docs are realigned to match the implementation: the envelope
table drops phantom task-lifecycle rows that never existed in code, the
mirror diagram in tasks.md is redrawn to show the actual update_task
RPC flow, the partial-quorum claim in hub.md is downgraded to a future
ambition, and WsLink reconnect-with-backoff is acknowledged across
transport.md and the design plan as a tenant concern rather than a
framework commitment.

11 new tests cover the mirror bridge, the cancel verb's success and
error paths, and the new hub accessors. Full beta suite stays green
(2407 passed).

fix(beta/network): make hub envelope ids strictly monotonic (#2941)

The per-(agent, channel) delivery cursor and reconnect replay compare
envelope ids lexicographically, so envelope ids must sort in creation
order. make_id() built ids as time.time_ns() + 8 random bytes, which
only sort by creation order while the wall clock strictly advances.

On coarse-resolution clocks (Windows, ~15 ms) two envelopes minted in
the same tick share the 8-byte time prefix and then sort by their random
suffix, non-deterministically. The cursor can advance to the wrong
envelope and replay can skip or re-send messages. Windows-only and
intermittent (depends on whether two posts land in the same tick);
Linux/macOS have nanosecond clocks so consecutive calls almost always
advance.

Add _MonotonicIds, a per-Hub callable that clamps each timestamp to
strictly above the previous one (the UUIDv7 monotonicity guarantee), and
mint every envelope id through it. State is per-instance (no module
global) and lock-guarded, so separate hubs and tests never share a
counter. As a side benefit, ordering now also survives a backwards
wall-clock step (NTP slew), which the old scheme did not.

Also mint the channel-close envelope inside the WAL lock so its id is
assigned in append order (it was minted before acquiring the lock), and
correct the stale "Envelope ids are UUID7" comment.

Regression test freezes the id clock, posts many envelopes in one tick,
and asserts the WAL stays sorted and the cursor tracks the head; it fails
reliably without the fix.

and that the Toolkit/Plugin compose multiple runtimes via last-to-first chain

* feat(beta/skills): runtime-owned read/execute + multi-runtime composition

Reshape the local-skills subsystem around the ADR-0005 design:

- SkillMetadata becomes pure frontmatter; add Skill/Script/Resource pure
  descriptors. A resource is any file that is not SKILL.md and not under
  scripts/ (disjoint from scripts), so scripts are no longer advertised as
  readable resources.
- SkillRuntime owns IO: skills/read/read_resource/execute. LocalRuntime moves
  the execution mechanics (shebang/chmod/command/sandbox) and resource
  resolution in; list-based lookup replaces the path-traversal guards. Each
  raises SkillNotFoundError when it does not own the named skill.
- SkillsToolkit and SkillPlugin accept *runtimes and route by last-to-first
  chain delegation, falling through only on SkillNotFoundError, so project
  skills shadow global ones across catalog, routing, and gating. SkillPlugin
  gates read_skill_resource / run_skill_script on whether any skill has
  resources / scripts (no dead tools).

fix(beta/network): fail fast when delegate targets self (#2998)

The `delegate` tool opens a one-shot consulting channel with the resolved
target. Consulting requires a respondent distinct from the initiator, so when
the target resolves to the calling agent itself the single participant
collapses both roles and the consulting adapter rejects the open with the
opaque `consulting requires exactly one respondent`. In multi-agent pipelines
where an LLM occasionally picks its own name as the delegate target, this
surfaces intermittently as a cryptic tool error and a stalled run.

Short-circuit in `delegate` before opening the channel: if the target agent_id
equals this agent's own id, return an actionable `cannot delegate to self`
error the model can recover from, and avoid creating a doomed channel.

* docs(beta): record Agent.run scoped-turn ADR and invocation glossary

ADR 0005: Agent.run is the non-blocking counterpart to Agent.ask. Its

authoritative idempotent outcome, and async iteration is a pure event
feed. Adds the agent-invocation context glossary and context map.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(beta): add observable Agent.run / AgentReply.run alongside ask

Adds an observable, non-blocking counterpart to `ask`. `agent.run(...)` (and
`reply.run(...)` for continuations) returns an `AgentRun` async context manager:
entering it opens the turn *scope* (middlewares + subscribers live) but does not
advance the turn; `await run.result()` drives it inline and returns the
`AgentReply`. Observation is push-based via `run.stream` — no background task.

Refactors the turn machinery so `run` is the single launch primitive: the setup
half of the loop is extracted into a `_turn_scope` async context manager that
yields a `drive` callable. `ask` / `_ask` / `resume` / `_execute` (and thus the
A2A executor + `AgentReply.ask`) all funnel through it, removing the duplicated
context-building and turn-driving.

ADR 0005 records the scoped, drive-on-result design.

* feat(network): add Hub.register(agent) convenience with per-agent client lifecycle

Lift HubClient.register onto the Hub so attaching an agent no longer
requires wiring a LocalLink + HubClient by hand:

    client = await hub.register(agent)   # -> AgentClient
    ...
    await client.close()                 # unregister + close its connection
    await hub.close()                    # closes any left open

Each hub.register() call mints a dedicated HubClient (default LocalLink,
or a supplied link=), owned by the returned AgentClient; the hub tracks
them and drains any still open on close(). AgentClient.close() closes the
transport only for hub-owned handles — in the explicit HubClient flow the
connection is shared/caller-owned, so close() there only unregisters.

The old low-level Hub.register(passport, resume) -> Passport is hard-renamed
to Hub.register_identity(...); internal callers, the register RPC, and 6
test files updated accordingly. The explicit HubClient(link, hub=hub) flow
is unchanged.

* feat(beta): add AgentRun.start() to drive a turn in the background

Adds an explicit, non-blocking way to drive an observable turn so callers
can pull events via run.stream.join() without the boilerplate
asyncio.create_task(run.result()).

AgentRun now drives the turn through a single scope-owned asyncio.Task,
created lazily by start() or result(). This collapses the previous
inline/background split (and its __driven/__reply/__error bookkeeping)
onto one path: idempotency and "re-raise the same failure" fall out of
awaiting the same task, and __aexit__ cancels it if still running so the
turn never outlives the block.

entering the block does not auto-start the turn still holds; the
"no background task" mechanism (driving inline in the caller's task) is
superseded. Updates the run docs to use run.start().

test(beta): Fix flaky discussion round-robin smoke test (#3015)

* test(anthropic): de-flake discussion round-robin smoke tests

test_discussion_round_robin_three_real_agents intermittently failed
with "Timeout (>45.0s) from pytest-timeout" while OpenAI/Gemini passed,
and while the 5-way discussion (more LLM calls) passed in ~4.6s — so it
is a flaky test, not a provider outage.

Two fragilities:

1. The test polled with timeout=60.0 but the suite-wide pytest-timeout
   is 45s (pyproject.toml), so the internal budget was dead code and the
   test was always signal-killed at 45s. Four sequential real LLM
   round-trips legitimately need more headroom; add @pytest.mark.timeout
   per the existing convention (image-gen/zai use the same), and drop the
   poll budget just under it so a stall reports the order assertion
   instead of a signal kill.

2. Thin prompts ("Reply briefly in one sentence" + "say hello") risked an
   empty reply, which posts no envelope (default_build_round_envelope
   returns None) and dead-stalls the rotation forever. Give each agent a
   concrete opinion to state so every turn yields substantive text.

Also add @pytest.mark.timeout(120) to test_5way_discussion_round_robin,
which had the same latent 90s-poll-vs-45s-cap mismatch.

ci: build docs only on manual dispatch or published release (#3036)

* ci: build docs only on manual dispatch or published release

Replace the push-to-main (path-filtered) trigger on the docs deploy
workflow with release: published, keeping workflow_dispatch. This stops
docs from rebuilding/redeploying on every push to main and aligns with
the faststream docs_build pattern.

Since build-mkdocs.yml is shared with the build-only PR check, add an
explicit `deploy` input (default false) and gate the gh-pages publish
steps on it instead of github.ref. On a release event github.ref is the
tag, so the old `github.ref == refs/heads/main` guards would have built
without deploying; the input decouples the publish decision from the ref.

ci: upload one combined coverage report per run instead of per matrix job (#3037)

Each matrix job in test.yml (5 Python versions x ubuntu + macos + windows)
and llm-test.yml (4 providers + mixed) called the Codecov action directly,
so a single PR produced 7+ separate Codecov uploads/reports.

Switch to the aggregate-then-upload pattern: every test job now stores its
binary .coverage file as an artifact, and a new `coverage-combine` job
downloads all of them, runs `coverage combine` + `coverage xml`, and performs
a single Codecov upload after every matrix job has finished.

`relative_files` so paths are stored relative to the repo root with normalized
separators. The coverage config is moved from the standalone .coveragerc into
[tool.coverage.run] in pyproject.toml (pytest-cov pulls in coverage[toml], so
the table is read on every Python version), and codecov.yml is relocated to
.github/codecov.yml (an auto-discovered location).

fix(test): de-flake test_cancelling_result_cancels_turn_inline (#3042)

The test gave the turn a fixed 0.2s (asyncio.wait_for) to reach the
blocking tool before cancelling. On GitHub's ubuntu runners with the
py3.14 toolcache build, coverage + full-suite conditions push turn
startup past that deadline, so the tool never starts and its
CancelledError handler can never run — failing the assertion
deterministically on CI while cancellation propagation itself is fine.

Gate the cancel on the tool actually being in flight instead: the tool
sets a `started` event, the test drives result() as a task, waits for
`started`, then cancels and expects CancelledError. Same property under
test (result() drives the turn inline; cancelling that await cancels
the in-flight turn), no wall-clock dependency, and faster (~30ms vs
always paying the 0.2s timeout).

fix: stop swallowing failures (silent data loss) (#3009)

* fix(beta): stop swallowing failures across subagents, tools, network, and eval

Four paths where an error vanished silently and the
system proceeded on wrong state.

- subagents: a failed delegated sub-task returned "" to the parent LLM;
  now returns a non-empty error string with the worker name and error.
- tools/executor: one raising tool call discarded the whole batch; now
  gathers with return_exceptions=True and converts a per-call exception
  into a ToolErrorEvent so the rest of the batch still returns.
- network/hub: _handle_endpoint swallowed dispatch failures with
  `except Exception: pass`; now logs via logger.exception before cleanup.
- eval/runtime: a single ref/agent failure crashed the entire run; both
  gathers now represent a failure as an error Trace (counted in aggregates)
  instead of discarding the run.

* test(beta): drop monkeypatching in eval failure tests; cover runner cancellation

* refactor(beta): extract shared gather-settling helper for eval runtime

* test(beta): rewrite silent-failure tests to use the public API

Replace internal patching in the silent-failure tests with public-API
equivalents, per review:

- runner: drive the failing task through a tool that raises (TestConfig)
  instead of monkeypatching runner._produce_one
- hub: register a LinkEndpoint whose frames() raises via the public
  attach_endpoint() instead of assigning over hub._dispatch_frame and
  calling hub._handle_endpoint() directly

Document the rule in test/beta/AGENTS.md: no monkeypatching internals;
inject failures through public seams (TestConfig, a raising tool, a
LinkEndpoint Protocol double).

* test(beta): drive silent-failure tests through the public ag2.testing seam

* refactor: simplify tool execution

* chore: clarify comments

fix(test): guard tool_search tests against single-provider CI envs (#3100)

The LLM test matrix installs one provider SDK per job, so any test module
that imports a provider SDK at import time — directly or via
`ag2.config.{provider}` — fails *collection* for the entire run, even when
the test itself is deselected by the `-m` marker. All four jobs (openai,
gemini, anthropic, zai) aborted with "Interrupted: N errors during
collection".

The tool_search tests added in #3032 landed in `test/beta/config/...`, a
path retired by #3023 when `autogen.beta` was promoted. That directory has
no `__init__.py`, so it missed the `pytest.importorskip(...)` guard that
`test/config/{provider}/__init__.py` provides:

- move the three provider tests into `test/config/{anthropic,openai}/tools/`
- guard the cross-provider `test/tools/test_tool_search_integration.py`
  with explicit `pytest.importorskip` calls, matching `test_mcp.py`

`test/AGENTS.md` still documented the pre-#3023 `test/beta/` layout, which
is what pointed the tests at the wrong directory. Update those paths and
document the importorskip requirement so this does not recur.

Verified by simulating each single-provider job with the other SDKs hidden
from the import system: no tool_search collection errors remain, and all
14 tests still pass when both SDKs are present.

fix(test): run the ACP test suite in CI and fix its Windows failure (#3103)

test/acp/__init__.py guards the package with pytest.importorskip("acp"),
but ag2[acp] was not in the `optionals` dependency group that the test
workflow installs. All 54 ACP tests were therefore silently skipped on
every CI run, and codecov reported 0% patch coverage for ag2/acp.

Adding ag2[acp] to `optionals` makes them run, which immediately exposed
a latent Windows failure in test_terminal_kill: it asserts the killed
process reports a signal, but Windows has no signals -- kill() maps to

correctly reports exit_code instead. The product behaviour is right; the
assertion was POSIX-only. Assert per-platform rather than skipping, so the
test still covers Windows.

Verified in a CI-shaped venv (uv pip install --group=test
--group=optionals -e .):
  without agent-client-protocol:   8 skipped
  with it:                        54 passed
Full suite under the CI marker filter: 3323 passed, 6 skipped, 1 xfailed.
The Windows branch itself can only be verified by CI.

* Remove unnecessary comment

* fix(acp): serve the tool gateway under an unguessable path

GATEWAY_PATH was the fixed constant "/mcp", so the only secret protecting
the gateway was the port number -- which `lsof -i -P | grep LISTEN` returns
instantly. Host/Origin validation does not close this: it stops a browser
page (which cannot forge Host) reaching the port via DNS rebinding, but a
local process sets whatever headers it likes. Any process on the machine
could therefore list and execute the agent's tools.

Mount the gateway under "/mcp/<secrets.token_urlsafe(32)>" instead. The URL
already travels to the CLI agent inside mcp_servers.url and appears nowhere
else: uvicorn's access log is off, and it is never a command-line argument
(it goes over the ACP stdio JSON-RPC in session/new). No new request
handler, no header plumbing, and it works with any MCP-over-HTTP client
rather than depending on adapters forwarding an Authorization header.

Verified live against both shipped adapters (claude-agent-acp and
codex-acp, via npx): tools still resolve and execute. A separate OS process
that knows the port but requests /mcp/ now gets 404 instead of executing
the tool.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(acp): make ACPConfig an async context manager

An ACP session outlives the agent.run() that created it -- reply.ask()
continues the same session, subprocess and tool gateway -- so the config's
scope, not the run's, is the conversation's lifetime. Nothing reclaims a
session implicitly: the weakref.finalize on context.stream only terminates
the subprocess, and it cannot fire anyway while config._sessions ->
ACPSession -> bridge.state.context -> stream keeps the stream reachable.

Before this, correct cleanup meant a try/finally opening above agent.run()
and closing below the last reply.ask() -- inverted from how the code reads,
since agent.run() is itself a context manager. Getting it wrong is silent:
the subprocess stays up and, with tools exposed, so does a listening MCP
server per session.

`async with ClaudeCodeConfig(...) as config:` now scopes that correctly,
including when the block raises. `await config.aclose()` is unchanged.

Docs: the Lifecycle section claimed "a finalizer terminates them as a safety
net if you don't", which is not true -- replaced with the async with pattern
and an explicit note that teardown is required. The tools example built a
config inline with no teardown, i.e. the exact leaking shape, in the section
introducing tool exposure.

Verified live against both shipped adapters (claude-agent-acp and codex-acp,
via npx): a tool call inside the scope works, reply.ask() after agent.run()
exits reuses the same session and gateway, and on scope exit the gateway
port is closed and the session registry empty -- including when the block
raises.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(acp): quiet deliberate shutdown, map incremental plans, guard name clash

Three follow-ups from review, plus a docs note.

Shutdown noise: timeout_graceful_shutdown cancels in-flight requests by
design, and uvicorn reports that at ERROR with a full ASGI traceback -- on
the path that is working correctly. A hung-tool run that behaved exactly as
intended (turn returned at 26.9s under turn_timeout=25, aclose() 5.2s, port
closed, exit 0) printed 4 such lines, which read as a crash. uvicorn.error is
a fixed logger name so it cannot be scoped per instance; mute it only for the
bounded duration of our own close().

Incremental plans: acp 0.11 added plan_update/plan_removed and both were
added to the SessionUpdate union, but map_session_update had no branch for
them, so they returned None and never reached the stream. The `items` payload
carries the same entries as the legacy `plan` update and now maps to ACPPlan.
`file`/`markdown`/`plan_removed` carry no ACPPlan-shaped payload and are left
unmapped -- but every unmapped update is now logged at debug (excluding
usage_update, which map_usage consumes by design) so a protocol addition is
visible rather than silently dropped. Measured: claude-agent-acp 0.62 still
emits the legacy `plan` form, so this is a latent path, not a live gap.

Name clash: the gateway is always registered as "ag2" (client.py never passed
ToolGateway's name=). An agent with function tools plus
MCPServerTool(server_label="ag2") sent two identically-named entries to
session/new with no error. ACP defines no precedence and agents namespace
tools as mcp__<name>__<tool>, so one set would silently shadow the other.
Rejected where the gateway's existence is known, so an external "ag2" server
remains valid when no gateway is built.

Verified live against claude-agent-acp and codex-acp: lifecycle scenarios
4/4 PASS on both, plan events still flow (14 ACPPlan in a planning task),
and the hung-tool path now prints 0 traceback lines instead of 4.

fix(events): preserve Enum types across serialization round-trip (#3102)

* fix(events): preserve Enum types across serialization round-trip

Enums were serialized to their bare value with no deserialization
counterpart, so BinaryInput.kind degraded to a plain str after
EventLogWriter persist/load and crashed the OpenAI mappers on
enum-identity checks and .value access.

Serialize enums with an __enum__ marker (same pattern as __bytes__,
__uuid__, __dataclass__) and restore them in deserialize_value. Harden
the OpenAI mappers to accept the raw strings still present in logs
persisted before this fix: str-enum equality instead of identity, and
error messages that no longer assume an enum.

Fixes #3084

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(events): fail open when an __enum__ class cannot be resolved

_resolve_class raises ImportError for an enum whose class can no longer be
imported -- built inside a factory, living in a plugin the reading process
lacks, or renamed between write and read. EventLogWriter._load_file catches
that and swaps the event for UnknownEvent, which the mappers then drop
without a warning, so a single unresolvable enum silently erases a whole
turn along with any attachment it carried. Before the __enum__ marker the
same value degraded to a plain string and the event still loaded.

Degrade to the raw value instead -- it is already in the payload. ValueError
covers the other half: a member removed from the enum since the log was
written. This also retires the bare assert, which is stripped under -O.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(events): coerce BinaryInput/UrlInput kind from pre-1.0 event logs

Logs written by 1.0.0b0 store kind as the bare string "image". On reload the
mappers identity-check against BinaryType and then read .kind.value on the
fall-through, so a resumed conversation carrying a persisted image crashes on
anthropic, bedrock and the a2a history mapper, and in events.sizing. Worse,
dashscope, ollama and gemini check `is BinaryType.IMAGE` with no .value on the
fall-through, so they never raise -- they silently drop the attachment and the
model simply never sees it.

Hardening the mappers means ~25 call sites across 7 files, each needing both
the .value fix and `is` -> `==`, or a crash is traded for a silent drop.
Coerce once at the source instead. Unrecognised values pass through untouched
so a log stays loadable.

This is a stopgap for one field of one type. The general problem -- event
reconstruction does not restore declared field types, and default=str in
EventLogWriter._serialize_events silently corrupts anything without a wire
marker -- is tracked as a follow-up. Both this and the mapper edits in the
preceding commit become removable once that lands.

The diagnosis that coercion belongs at reconstruction rather than in the
mappers came from @Solaris-star in #3091.

fix(beta/subagents): accept Stream instance in `as_tool(stream=...)` and reject invalid types loudly (#2893)

* fix(subagents): accept Stream instance in as_tool(stream=)

as_tool / subagent_tool only accepted a StreamFactory
(Callable[[Agent, Context], Stream]). Passing a bare Stream instance
fell through: the call site stream(agent, ctx) either misread the
instance as a factory and crashed, or the guard returned None so the
sub-agent ran with a fresh ephemeral stream and the caller's stream
stayed empty -- the caller could never capture sub-agent events.

Add a StreamOrFactory alias (Stream | StreamFactory) and resolve the
argument once at tool-construction time: a Stream instance is wrapped in
a factory returning that exact instance, a callable is treated as a
factory as before, None keeps the per-call default, and anything else
raises TypeError eagerly instead of silently producing an empty stream.

Closes #3021. Adds regression tests for the instance, factory, None and
invalid-type paths.

* fix(beta/subagents): apply the stream= contract to background_agent_tool

`background_agent_tool` accepted the same `stream=` parameter as
`subagent_tool` but still called it as a factory, so a `Stream` instance
raised `TypeError: 'MemoryStream' object is not callable` when the tool
ran — inside a spawned background task, where it is hard to attribute.
It now shares `_resolve_stream_argument`, and `_run_and_deliver` takes a
`Stream` rather than a `MemoryStream`.

`_resolve_stream_argument` also rejects a `Stream` class passed where an
instance was meant. A Stream class satisfies the runtime-checkable
`Stream` protocol, so `stream=MemoryStream` was reused as if it were an
instance and failed deep in the run.

Document that a shared `Stream` instance makes the sub-agent stateful:
each delegation sees every earlier delegation's turns, with token cost
to match. Adds a "Shared Stream Instance" section to the subagents user
guide, and tests covering the background path, the class rejection, and
the stateful/isolated split.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Drop the issue reference and the account of the pre-fix failure mode from

fix(docs): ship robots.txt so it stops advertising the /latest archive (#3115)

robots.txt sat at website/mkdocs/robots.txt, outside docs_dir, so mkdocs never
copied it into the build. The deploy in build-mkdocs.yml only overlays gh-pages
(cp -r, no delete), so the pre-1.0 file has survived every deploy and the live
https://docs.ag2.ai/robots.txt still reads:

    Disallow: /0.
    Sitemap: https://docs.ag2.ai/latest/sitemap.xml

That advertises the removed-versioning archive to crawlers, which is a large
part of why /latest outranks the current docs. The old Disallow never matched
/latest either.

Moving the file into docs_dir ships it and overwrites the stale copy. The
archives are left crawlable on purpose: every archived page now carries
<meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow">, and Googlebot has to fetch a
page to see it. A Disallow would hide the noindex and the URLs would linger.

fix(perplexity): read SDK response nodes that arrive as dicts (#3119)

perplexityai 0.43.0 refers to nested response models by string forward
reference inside PEP 585 aliases (`list["ChoiceOutput"]`). Python 3.10's
`typing._eval_type` does not recurse into `types.GenericAlias` args, so
pydantic leaves those annotations unresolved and the SDK hands back raw
dicts for `choices` and `search_results` where 3.11+ gets models.

Reading those nodes by attribute therefore dropped `content` and raised
`AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'title'` on 3.10. Read
them through a helper that accepts either shape, so parsing no longer
depends on the SDK's model construction.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(contributing): document the optionals dependency group for Extensions (#3126)

The Extension contribution policy explains how to declare third-party
packages (additional dependencies guarded by `missing_additional_dependency`)
but never mentions adding them to the `optionals` dependency group in
pyproject.toml, which is what the test workflow installs:

    uv pip install --system --group=test --group=optionals -e .

Read together with "not as pyproject extras", this reads as "don't touch
pyproject at all". The result is an Extension whose tests are guarded by
`pytest.importorskip(...)` and are therefore skipped on every CI run — the
Extension ships untested and CI still passes.

The only place the group is currently explained is a comment inside
pyproject.toml, which is not somewhere a contributor would look.

Adds the missing step to the policy and mirrors it in AGENTS.md, plus a
note on dependency footprint: `optionals` resolves as a single environment,
so a package with heavy or loosely-bounded transitive dependencies can
downgrade shared packages for unrelated tests.

fix(spec): warn on unknown fields in AgentSpec instead of dropping them silently (#3118)

* fix(spec): reject unknown fields in AgentSpec instead of dropping them silently

* fix(spec): warn on unknown spec fields instead of dropping them silently

Pydantic ignores unrecognised keys by default, so a misspelled
`tool_nammes` produced a spec that validated cleanly and built an agent
with no tools, with no signal anywhere.

Warns rather than raising, so this is not a breaking change and a spec
written against a newer AG2 still loads. The message names each unknown
key and suggests the closest valid field, which is what makes the typo
case self-diagnosing.

Strict mode needs no new API — the standard warning filters do it:

    warnings.simplefilter("error", UnknownSpecFieldWarning)

If we later want unknown fields to be an error by default, this is the
deprecation step that gives users notice first.

The description types, the opt-in protocol and the builtin implementations

feat(agent): expose composition as public read-only properties (#3134)

Building a custom dumper, comparing two agents, or asserting on
composition in a test all required reading private attributes. This adds
the fields those callers actually need:

  Agent      system_prompt, dynamic_prompt, middleware, dependencies,
             variables, response_schema, observers, tasks, assembly
  Tool       middleware
  Middleware cls, options

Sequences return tuples and mappings return read-only views, so an agent
cannot be mutated through them.

agent.middleware and tool.middleware yield DescribedMiddleware entries,
each pairing the middleware object with its description. Entries are
built on access, so the execution path is untouched and the middleware
inside is the real object: a description says what a middleware is, and
identity says whether two tools share one. Ten tools holding a single
rate limiter and ten holding separate ones with identical settings
produce equal descriptions, so identity is the only thing that
distinguishes them.

Middleware.options exposes option values while describe() reports only
their names. A description may be logged or committed as a fixture;
reading a factory you already hold is a deliberate act.

Prompt hooks now carry their identity through the wrapper, so
dynamic_prompt yields nameable hooks rather than anonymous wrappers.

* fix(tools): report sub-task usage incurred before a failure

run_task's success path computes TaskResult.usage from the usage events

fix(policies): never trim a builtin tool call away from its reasoning item (#3150)

* fix(policies): never trim a builtin tool call away from its reasoning item

SlidingWindowPolicy and TokenBudgetPolicy cut at an arbitrary event index,
so the cut could land between a reasoning item and the server-side tool call
it anchors. The surviving web_search_call was then replayed without its
required reasoning item and the request failed with a 400.

ensure_tool_pairing does not cover this: it matches results against
ModelResponse.tool_calls, and server-side tool calls never appear there.
Their invariant is a reasoning anchor, not a call/result pair.

Add safe_cut(), which moves a trim point forward past a group split by the
cut, stopping at the next group's own anchor. Advancing only removes events,
so TokenBudgetPolicy still holds its budget.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(policies): implement replay invariants for history reduction

Introduce a new replay mechanism to ensure that history reduction
(via compaction or assembly policies) never leaves orphaned events that
would cause provider API errors.

Specifically, this change ensures that the following event pairings
are always preserved:
- Tool results are always accompanied by their corresponding tool calls.
- Builtin (server-side) tool calls are always accompanied by their
  associated reasoning items.
- Local call events are always accompanied by the ModelResponse that
  announced them.

Key changes:
- Added `ag2/_replay.py` to provide logic for calculating valid
  replayable spans and snapping boundaries.
- Refactored `ag2/compact.py` to use the new `snap` utility for
  maintaining event integrity during compaction.
- Updated `SlidingWindowPolicy` and `TokenBudgetPolicy` to use
  `replayable_span`, ensuring they drop orphaned events rather than
  leaving them in the window.
- Removed the deprecated `ag2/policies/_pairing.py`.
- Updated documentation to explain that reduction limits (max events/tokens)
  are targets rather than strict guarantees due to these invariants.
- Added comprehensive tests for builtin tool boundaries, reasoning
  anchors, and window widening behavior.

* fix(middleware): apply replay invariants to history and token limiters

Integrate the replay invariant logic into `HistoryLimiter` and `TokenLimiter`
to prevent provider errors caused by orphaned builtin tool calls.

This ensures that both middleware and assembly policies respect the
requirement that builtin tool calls must be accompanied by their
corresponding reasoning items.

Key changes:
- Refactored `HistoryLimiter` and `TokenLimiter` to use `replayable_span`
  from `ag2._replay`.
- Updated `_replay.py` to reset the reasoning anchor at `ModelRequest`
  and `ModelResponse` boundaries, preventing anchor leakage across
  different turns.
- Updated documentation to clarify that `max_events` and `max_tokens`
  are targets rather than strict guarantees due to these invariants.
- Added regression tests for `HistoryLimiter` and `TokenLimiter` to
  verify that builtin tool groups are preserved during trimming.

docs(middleware): correct tool middleware sharing claims and document the shared-budget pattern (#3136)

* fix(tools): keep tool middleware shared when a tool is copied

Attaching one middleware instance to several tools is how you give them a
combined allowance: a budget of 3 across 10 tools should permit 3 calls in
total, not 30. That worked for closures and silently broke for class
instances.

FunctionTool.ensure_tool deepcopies any Tool passed to Agent(tools=[...]),
and the copy took the tool's _middleware tuple with it. copy.deepcopy treats
functions as atomic and returns the same object, but duplicates class
instances -- so a stateful hook became N independent copies, none of them the
object the caller was holding. No error, no warning; the effective limit was
just multiplied by the number of tools.

Give Tool a __deepcopy__ that copies the tool but carries _middleware across
by reference. Middleware is behaviour attached to a tool, not state belonging
to it. This follows the existing opt-out precedent: DockerEnvironment,
DaytonaEnvironment and their sandboxes already return self from __deepcopy__
so that Agent.add_tool can copy a tool backed by a shared resource handle.

ApprovalRequired is the only class-based tool middleware AG2 ships, and it
keeps its state in context.variables rather than on the instance, which is
why the defect never surfaced in the test suite.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(middleware): correct tool middleware sharing claims

A hook instance attached to several tools is not shared. Registering a
tool deep-copies it, which duplicates a class-based hook while leaving a
plain function shared, so a budget kept on the instance silently becomes
one budget per tool. The docstrings added in #3134 and the new mdx
example stated the opposite; verified across every registration path:
Agent(tools=[...]) and Toolkit both copy, only ask(tools=[...]) shares.

Point shared state at context.dependencies instead: values are passed by
reference into every run and into sub-tasks, and are never copied or
serialised, so the number of hook copies stops mattering. The hook keeps
only its settings and stays describable.

Drops the Tool.__deepcopy__ change — the combined-allowance use case is
expressible without altering copy semantics for every tool.

refactor(acp): implement in-order update handling and remove manual settling (#3175)

The SDK (since 0.12.1) now guarantees completeness by not returning from
`session/prompt` until all in-flight `session/update` handlers have
returned. This allows the removal of manual settling logic and timeouts
in the client.

However, the SDK spawns a new task for every notification, which allows
`session/update` handlers to interleave. This can cause streamed chunks
to arrive out of order. This change replaces the previous queue-based
dispatcher with an `asyncio.Lock` based approach in `InOrderUpdates` to
ensure that handlers are executed sequentially in the order they were
received from the wire.

- Replace `InboundUpdates` with `InOrderUpdates` in `ACPBridge`.
- Remove `_UPDATE_SETTLE_TIMEOUT` and manual `settle()` calls in `Client`.
- Remove `_dispatch_kwargs` as the SDK now handles completeness.

feat(acp): let a host answer a served agent's human-input request (#3177)

`ACPAgent` hard-wired human input to a rejection: every `context.input()`
in an ACP-driven turn failed, and a hosting application that *does* have a
way to reach its user — its own chat surface, an approval queue, a ticket —
had no seam to supply it.

Add `ACPAgent(..., hitl_hook=...)`, passed through to `AgentExecutor` and
on to `Agent._execute`. It is an ordinary AG2 HITL hook: same shape as
`Agent(hitl_hook=...)`, sync or async, dependency injection included. `None`
keeps today's behaviour exactly, and the served agent's own hook stays
overridden — a hook written for `agent.ask()` typically reads a console, and
over stdio the console is the protocol.

This is deliberately protocol-invisible: no capability is advertised and no
ACP method is called. Client-driven approvals still need ACP elicitation on
this side, which remains unwired.

Also fixes the rejection path itself. `_reject_human_input` took an
un-annotated `context` parameter, which a hook resolves as another *field* to
fill from the event — so the turn died of a pydantic validation error naming
the private function rather than `HumanInputUnsupportedError`. The error the
class exists to raise never actually reached a client.

refactor: annotate contextmanager returns as Generator, not Iterator (#3176)

that accepts `Iterator[T]` / `AsyncIterator[T]` as deprecated, so pyright
1.1.409+ flags 31 sites in this repo. The warning is worth acting on
rather than silencing: `_AsyncGeneratorContextManager.__aexit__` calls
`gen.athrow()`, so the decorator needs a real generator. The iterator
annotation is an under-specification — it type-checks, while a

Rewrites the return annotation at all 31 decorated functions (27 async,

fix(subagents): reuse one stream object in persistent_stream() (#3160)

* fix(subagents): reuse one stream object in persistent_stream()

The factory cached only the stream id in context.dependencies and built a
fresh MemoryStream on every delegation. Agent._execute serializes turns
through a lock attached to the stream instance itself, so two delegations
into the same persistent sub-agent got two distinct locks and the
serialization silently did not apply - concurrent turns could overlap and
cross-register subscribers.

Cache the MemoryStream itself now, so all delegations in a context share one
object (setdefault keeps concurrent first delegations consistent). Update
the run_task comment that described the old rebuild-per-call behavior, and
add tests asserting same-object reuse, including under asyncio.gather.

Closes #3123

* fix(agent): ensure stream serialization via stream ID instead of object identity

Refactor the stream turn locking mechanism to use the stream's unique ID
rather than the Python object instance. This ensures that concurrent
turns on the same logical stream are correctly serialized even if the
`Stream` object is reconstructed (e.g., via `persistent_stream()` or
resuming a session from storage).

Changes:
- Implement `_stream_locks_by_id` using a `weakref.WeakValueDictionary`
  to manage per-ID `asyncio.Lock` instances.
- Update `_get_stream_turn_lock` to prioritize the stream ID for lock
  lookup, while still caching the lock on the instance for performance.
- Update `persistent_stream` to cache the `stream_id` in context
  dependencies instead of the `MemoryStream` object itself.
- Update tests to verify that serialization holds true for both shared
  object instances and distinct objects sharing the same ID.

* feat(mcp): upgrade to MCP 2.0 and update handler registration

Migrate the MCP implementation from the 1.x decorator-based API to the 2.0
constructor-callback pattern. This includes updating all core providers
(tools, prompts, and resources) to use the new `on_*` handler signatures
and `ServerRequestContext`.

Key changes:
- Update `MCPServer` and `ToolGateway` to use `Server` constructor callbacks
  instead of `@server.call_tool` style decorators.
- Refactor `AgentExecutor` and `MCPToolkit` to handle the new `CallToolResult`
  model and snake_case attribute naming (e.g., `is_error`, `input_schema`).
- Implement manual input validation in `MCPFunctionTool` using `jsonschema`
  to maintain parity with 1.x behavior, as 2.0 removes automatic validation.
- Update `mcp-ui` resource builders to handle the retyped `str` URI format.
- Update `pyproject.toml` to require `mcp>=2.0.0,<3` and add `jsonschema`.
- Update testing utilities to use `create_client_server_memory_streams` for
  compatibility with the new 2.0 client object structure.
- Fix typos in documentation and code snippets (e.g., `streamable_http_client`).

* refactor(mcp): improve error handling and resource validation

Refactor the MCP implementation to provide more robust error reporting,
better logging, and stricter validation for UI resources.

Key changes:
- Improve tool error reporting by ensuring exception class names are
  returned when the exception string is empty.
- Add server-side logging for tool execution failures to preserve
  tracebacks that are otherwise lost over the wire.
- Refactor `ag2/acp/tool_gateway.py` to use a centralized `tool_error`
  helper for consistent error responses.
- Implement stricter URI validation in `mcp_ui` using a shared
  `_require_ui_uri` guard.
- Add validation for encoding types in `mcp_ui` resource builders.
- Enable `follow_redirects=True` in the `MCPToolkit` HTTP client to
  support Starlette's trailing slash redirects.
- Update test suites to cover edge cases for silent exceptions,
  invalid URIs, and redirect handling.

* Update uv.lock

fix: usage accounting sources (#3161)

* feat(eval): implement usage-based token accounting via `UsageEvent`

Transition token accounting from summing `ModelResponse` events to
aggregating `UsageEvent` records. This ensures that all billable work—
including sub-task rollups, history compaction, memory aggregation, and
live sessions—is accurately captured, even when it does not produce a
standard LLM span.

Changes:
- Introduce `UsageEvent` as the primary framework accounting record.
- Update `TelemetryMiddleware` to subscribe to usage events and emit
  dedicated `usage` spans.
- Refactor `TokenMonitor` to observe `UsageEvent` instead of
  `ModelResponse` or `TaskCompleted`.
- Update `Trace.tokens` to aggregate usage via `UsageReport`.
- Upgrade evaluation result schema from `0.1` to `0.2` to support the
  new accounting model.
- Add ADR 0014 documenting the decision to use `UsageEvent` for
  consistent token reporting across all consumers.

* refactor(telemetry): decouple usage recording from middleware lifecycle

Refactor the telemetry middleware to use weak references for usage
recording. This prevents memory leaks and ensures that usage events
from a previous run on a shared stream do not leak into subsequent
runs.

Additionally, simplify the `AG2GenAIConvention` by removing stateful
tracking of duplicated rollups. Instead, duplicate detection is now
handled during the trace reconstruction pass, making the convention
readers stateless and safer to reuse.

Changes:
- Implement `_make_usage_recorder` with `weakref` to bind subscriptions
  to the middleware instance lifecycle.
- Remove `duplicated_rollups` state from `AG2GenAIConvention`.
- Update `spans_to_trace` logic to handle rollup deduplication via
  value equality during the event pass.
- Update documentation and tests to reflect the stateless convention
  and improved subscription management.

* fix(eval): match rollup dedupe by agent name and apply trace adjustments to caller-supplied conventions

fix(hitl): fail the turn when nobody can answer a human-input request (#3179)

* fix(hitl): fail the turn when nobody can answer a human-input request

* fix(hitl): ensure human input failures terminate the turn and repair history

When a tool requires human input (via approval middleware or direct
context calls) and the input channel is unavailable or fails, the
current implementation often allowed the agent to continue as if the
tool had simply failed or timed out. This could lead to inconsistent
agent behavior, where the model attempts to "route around" a human
requirement that is actually unfulfillable.

This change ensures that a `HumanInputError` correctly terminates the
current turn across all surfaces (including ACP and MCP gateways) and
prevents the agent from continuing with a broken state.

Key changes:
- Implement `fail_channel` in ACP `Bridge` to propagate human input
  failures from the gateway back to the client.
- Update `ToolGateway` and `executor` to catch `HumanInputError` and
  trigger turn termination instead of reporting a standard tool error.
- Add `close_unanswered_tool_calls` to `history` to inject a
  `HUMAN_INPUT_ABANDONED_TOOL_RESULT` into the transcript. This
  prevents history corruption (unanswered tool calls) that causes
  LLM providers to reject subsequent turns.
- Update `approval_required` middleware to default `timeout` to `None`,
  allowing indefinite waiting for human input unless explicitly bounded.
- Improve `HumanInputError` serialization via `__reduce__` to ensure
  exception context is preserved when traveling across task boundaries.
- Add comprehensive tests for ACP, MCP, and sub-agent delegation
  scenarios to verify that unanswerable questions end the parent turn.
- Update documentation to reflect the new behavior regarding timeouts
  and history repair.
