feat(acp): implement session/load so a client can resume a conversation (#3222)

`ACPAgent` advertised `load_session=False`, so a client that reconnected
could not get its conversation back. For a host that spawns one agent
process per message — as AG2 Space's agent-connect does — that meant every
message started a memoryless conversation, and chat records fragmented one
per message with no way to regroup them afterwards.

The session id is now the stream id in hex, so the id a client is handed is
exactly the key its history is stored under. Nothing else about a session is
durable, and `session/load` re-supplies the rest (cwd, mcpServers,
additionalDirectories), so an id alone is enough to rehydrate a conversation
from storage — written by another connection, or another process.

`session/load` replays the whole transcript as `session/update` notifications
and returns only once the last one is delivered, per the protocol. Replay
reconstructs what the client saw from what the loop persisted: agent text
comes from `ModelResponse` (the streamed chunks are transient and never
stored), user turns are re-emitted as `user_message_chunk`, and a tool call
persisted three times with its result persisted twice is started once and
settled once. A turn cut short by a dead process is repaired first, gated on
whether a call is genuinely unanswered — a clean `final=True` turn leaves no
`ToolResultsEvent` wrapper, and healing it unconditionally would rewrite a
valid transcript on every load.

Retention is opt-in via `SessionConfig.retain_history` (default off, matching
today's behaviour). When on, connection teardown, LRU eviction and TTL expiry
release the live session without touching its history; an explicit `close()`
still deletes, since that is the act that means the conversation is over.
Loading is truthful about the rest: an id whose history is gone gets
`resource_not_found`, which is what a client already handles.

`ACPAgent(on_session=...)` tells a host when a session comes to exist, with
"created" after `session/new` and "loaded" after `session/load`, so an
application keying its own records by session id can bind them at the moment
the id exists. A hook that raises refuses the request and leaves nothing
behind — the adopted session is unregistered without deleting its history, so
a subsequent `session/prompt` answers `resource_not_found` rather than
finding a session the host declined to vouch for.

Two limits are documented rather than enforced, and both are stated in the
user guide: there is no cross-process lease, so one live process per session
id is the client's contract; and `ag2` never reclaims a retained history,
since `max_sessions` and `ttl` bound the live registry rather than the
storage behind it.

`session/resume`, `list`, `fork`, `close` and `delete` remain unadvertised.

* fix(telemetry): record structured and multi-part tool results on tool spans

`on_tool_execution` recorded `gen_ai.tool.call.result` only when
`result.result.parts[0]` was a `TextInput`, so a tool returning a dict, a
Pydantic model, or a list had its result omitted entirely, and a multi-part
result lost everything after the first part. `ag2.eval` rebuilds its `Trace`
from these spans, so judge and attribution scorers graded transcripts with
empty tool outputs.

binary/url/file parts as descriptors, multiple parts newline-joined. A lone
text part renders to the same plain string as before. The value is capped at
`MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS` (8192) with a `...[truncated]` marker and a companion
`ag2.tool.call.result.truncated` attribute.

fix(eval): count suite tasks with no trace instead of dropping them (#3227)

`evaluate_traces` built one `TaskResult` per `TraceRef`, so a suite task the
source had no trace for contributed nothing. `Aggregates` is computed over the
graded tasks, so the pass-rate denominator shrank instead of registering a
failure — a run that crashed before producing a trace made the suite look
better, not worse.

Adds a keyword-only `on_missing_task: Literal["error", "ignore", "raise"]`.
Default `"error"` grades the uncovered task with an empty `Trace` carrying a
new public `MissingTraceError`, through the normal scorer path, so it counts in
`aggregates.errors` and in the pass-rate denominator — mirroring what
`run_agent` already does for a task that raised. `"ignore"` is the old
behaviour plus a warning; `"raise"` aborts before grading. A trace whose
`task_id` is not in the suite is still graded reference-free.

fix(middleware): stop retries after streaming chunks (#3216)

* fix(middleware): stop retrying after streaming chunks

* fix(middleware): prevent retries after streaming output has been published

Modify `RetryMiddleware` to stop retrying if any event has been published
to the stream during an attempt. This prevents duplicate or
concatenated output in the stream when a transient error occurs after
the provider has already started streaming chunks, reasoning, or tool
calls.

Key changes:
- Replace type-specific `ModelMessageChunk` tracking with a generic
  `_RetryAttempt` interrupter that tracks any published `BaseEvent`.
- Update `RetryMiddleware` to check the `published` status of an
  attempt before deciding to retry.
- Expand test coverage to include various event types (reasoning,
  tool calls, etc.) that should trigger the retry suppression.
- Update documentation to explain the behavior regarding streaming
  clients and transient failures.

* refactor(middleware): simplify retry detection using stream state

Replace the custom `_RetryAttempt` interrupter class with a direct check
on the stream's published status. This streamlines the logic for
detecting if an LLM call has already emitted events (such as chunks,
reasoning, or tool calls) to the stream.

By using `context.stream.get(BaseEvent)` and checking `published.done()`,
the middleware can more reliably determine if a retry is safe or if
it would result in duplicate/concatenated output for live consumers.

- Remove `_RetryAttempt` helper class
- Use `async with context.stream.get(BaseEvent)` to monitor event emission
- Update tests to use explicit `Context` with `MemoryStream`
- Simplify documentation regarding streaming retry behavior

* test(testing): introduce Turn typealias and improve TestClient flexibility

Refactor the testing utilities to support more complex, multi-event
LLM turns. This change introduces a `Turn` typealias that allows
scripting sequences of events (strings, tool calls, base events, or
exceptions) to simulate realistic streaming and error scenarios.

Key changes:
- Add `Turn` typealias to `ag2.testing` to represent a single scripted
  LLM turn.
- Update `TestClient` to iterate through a sequence of `Turn` objects,
  allowing for mid-turn event emission (e.g., streaming chunks) before
  the final response.
- Improve `TestClient` logic to handle `BaseException` and `BaseEvent`
  types within a turn script.
- Refactor `test_llm_retry.py` to use the new `Turn`-based scripting
  approach, making retry middleware tests more expressive and robust.

* docs(docs): update middleware documentation regarding retry behavior

Clarify the conditions under which streaming calls are not retried.
The documentation now explicitly mentions that publishing chunks,
reasoning, or server-side tool calls prevents retries to avoid
duplicate output in the stream.

fix(middleware): record full history and tool-call output on chat spans (#3238)

* fix(middleware): record full history and tool-call output on chat spans

`gen_ai.input.messages` only recorded the current user message (TextInput
parts of ModelRequest events), and `gen_ai.output.messages` was skipped when
the model replied with tool calls and no text. On a tool-calling turn every
`chat` span therefore showed the same single user message as its input and
the first span had no output at all, so a trace could neither replay what the
model saw nor show which tool it chose.

Add `_build_input_messages()`, which walks the full event sequence handed to
`on_llm_call` and serialises it OpenAI-style: `user` for text inputs,
`assistant` (with `tool_calls`) for prior ModelResponse events, and `tool`
with `tool_call_id` for each ToolResultsEvent result. Tool results go through
the existing `_serialize_tool_result` so binary parts appear as descriptors
and the `max_tool_result_chars` cap applies as it does on tool spans. Non-text
user inputs are omitted. Emit `gen_ai.output.messages` whenever the response
carries a message or tool calls. Both attributes still respect
`capture_content`.

Revives closed PRs #2834 and #2835 on the current `ag2/` layout.

* feat(mcp): add support for MCP Apps and interactive documents

Implement the MCP Apps extension (SEP-2133) to allow agents to serve
interactive HTML documents alongside tools. This enables a parallel
rendering pattern where the host fetches a static resource via the
`ui://` scheme while simultaneously executing tool calls.

Key features:
- Introduced `AppResource` to bundle HTML documents with associated

- Added `MCPServer` support for the `apps` parameter, providing a
  shorthand for registering app-specific tools and resources.

  new MCP Apps workflow.

Update the user guide to provide more detailed technical information regarding
MCP Apps, the `ag2ui` global injection mechanism, and the behavior of
structured tool outputs.

Key documentation improvements:

- Document new `ag2ui.host` properties (`protocolVersion`, `info`) and
  the `ag2ui.reportSize()` method.
- Add guidance on the `ag2ui.ready` handshake requirement before making
  host calls.
- Explain the relationship and differences between MCP-UI and MCP Apps.

* refactor(mcp): consolidate test helpers and improve test suite structure

Refactor the MCP test suite to reduce duplication and improve maintainability
by centralizing common testing utilities and cleaning up redundant code.

Key changes:
- Introduce `test/mcp/_helpers.py` to provide shared utilities like
  `make_agent`, `text_of`, and `tool_named`.
- Remove redundant local helper functions (`_agent`, `_tool`, `_text`)
  across multiple test files.
- Standardize the use of Pydantic models and dataclasses in tests by
  moving them to the central helpers module.
- Improve test readability by using descriptive helper functions for
  asserting tool metadata and content extraction.
- Fix minor inconsistencies in how tool results and structured content
  are validated.

* feat(mcp): implement MCP Apps and request-scoped context resolution

Introduce support for MCP Apps (interactive documents) and enhance the
MCP implementation to support request-scoped variables, dependencies,
and context resolution within tools and resources.

- Rename `AppResource` to `MCPApp` and introduce `AppSandbox` for
  policy management.
- Add support for `AppContent` to include inline HTML, file paths,
  and `Variable` types.
- Implement `MCPExecutionContext` to manage request-scoped variables,
  dependencies, and prompts.
- Enable resolution of `Variable` and `Inject` annotations within
  MCP tool handlers and resource readers.
- Update `MCPServer` to handle `MCPApp` instances and integrate
  context providers for dynamic metadata and content.
- Add `MCPRequestContextField` to allow tools to access the live
  MCP request context via dependency injection.

* feat(mcp): enhance MCP Apps with request-scoped context resolution

Implement support for request-scoped variables and dependencies within
MCP Apps and resources. This allows document content, titles, and
metadata to be dynamically resolved per request using the server's
`context_provider`.

Key changes:
- Update `MCPApp` to support multiple content types: literal HTML,
  path-like files (re-read on every request), `Variable`s, and
  callables.
- Implement `MCPRequestContext` to allow tool and resource handlers
  to access request-specific metadata.

  `title`, `description`, and `mime_type`.
- Refactor `MCPExecutionContext` to focus on request-scoped values
  rather than conversational turn state.

  registration.
- Update documentation to reflect the new `MCPApp` API and the
  distinction between request-scoped and turn-scoped context.

feat(mcp): ask the calling client for input, and answer a server that asks (#3230)

* feat(mcp): implement elicitation and pause/resume for modern MCP protocol

Introduce support for the "modern era" MCP protocol (post 2026-07-28),
where server-to-client requests are replaced by returning
`InputRequiredResult` as a tool call result.

This implementation includes:
- A `pause` mechanism to hold suspended coroutines in-process between
  client rounds, using a `requestState` token to facilitate resumption.
- `elicitation` logic to route agent questions to the human behind the
  MCP client via `context.input()`.
- `AnswerPolicy` in the MCP toolkit to allow agents to respond to
  third-party MCP server requests (elicitation, sampling, and roots).
- Support for both "legacy" (handshake-era) and "auto" (modern-era)
  protocol modes via `ProtocolMode`.
- New error types for declined elicitation and improved session
  management to handle state eviction.

Added comprehensive tests for both handshake-era elicitation and
modern-era pause/resume workflows.

* feat(mcp): add sampling support and refine input/elicitation workflows

Introduce support for MCP sampling, allowing served agents to borrow
the calling client's model for reasoning. This implementation includes:

- `ClientModel` configuration to enable/disable model borrowing,
  shifting cost and capability to the caller.
- `MCPSamplingError` hierarchy to handle unavailable or refused
  sampling requests.
- Refined elicitation and pause/resume logic to better handle
  `InputRequiredResult` and `InputResponse` types across protocol eras.
- Enhanced `MCPFunctionTool` with support for deterministic tool
  parameter resolution via the SDK's resolver mechanism.
- Improved error handling in the toolkit to unwrap `ExceptionGroup`
  wrappers from `ClientSession` task groups.
- Updated documentation for both client-side answering and
  server-side serving of MCP requests.

Added comprehensive tests for client model borrowing, deterministic
tool input resolution, and lifecycle bounds for paused runs.

* fix(mcp): measure a paused run's retention from its newest state

Every round mints a fresh requestState, so a conversation that pauses
and resumes repeatedly could outlive the TTL in total while the token
its client holds was always young — and be reclaimed under a token the
boundary still accepts. PausedRuns.register now restamps the run.

Also drops PauseState.conversation, which was minted, encoded and
decoded but never read, and asserts the caller binding from the wire
rather than at the seam.

* feat(mcp): implement input request handling and refine elicitation/sampling

Enhance MCP support by implementing robust handling for input requests,
elicitation, and sampling. This includes support for modern MCP protocol
revisions where questions are returned as call results rather than
standalone requests.

Key changes:
- Implement `InputRequiredResult` handling to support modern MCP era
  (2026-07-28) where server-to-client requests are replaced by call
  results.
- Refine elicitation and sampling logic to ensure consistent behavior
  across protocol revisions.
- Improve error handling for sampling, specifically ensuring that
  unusable completions (e.g., missing text blocks) are refused loudly
  rather than treated as silence.
- Update documentation to reflect the implications of sticky routing,
  process-local state, and the differences between elicitation,
  sampling, and roots in terms of refusal mechanisms.
- Add comprehensive tests for paused run concurrency, stale answer
  rejection, and media block validation in sampling.
- Ensure `MCPServer` properly reclaims paused runs during shutdown.

* refactor(mcp): simplify client model configuration and fallback logic

Simplify the `client_model` API by allowing a boolean shorthand and
removing the redundant `fallback` parameter from `ClientModel`. The
fallback behavior is now implicitly determined by whether the agent
has its own model configuration.

Key changes:
- Update `MCPServer` to accept `bool | ClientModel` for `client_model`,
  where `True` enables borrowing the caller's model with default
  settings.
- Remove `fallback` attribute from `ClientModel`.
- Refactor fallback logic: if a client cannot sample, the server
  automatically falls back to the agent's own `config` if present,
  otherwise it raises `MCPSamplingUnavailableError`.
- Update error messages and documentation to reflect the new
  implicit fallback mechanism.
- Update tests to validate the boolean shorthand and the new
  fallback behavior.

* feat(mcp): implement input request handling and refine elicitation/sampling

This change implements support for MCP input requests (elicitation) and
sampling, allowing served agents to request human input or model
completions from the calling client.

Key changes:
- Implement `Elicit`, `Resolve`, and `Sample` request handling to support

Refactor docstrings and comments across the MCP test suite to be more

* feat(tealtiger): add output_scan governance policy

Scan tool RESULTS for PII/secrets before they flow back into agent context. Adds GovernancePolicy.output_scan(scan_pii, scan_secrets, pii_action, secret_action, categories) with per-detector REDACT/BLOCK/FLAG actions (default: redact PII, block secrets). Runs post-tool-execution in MONITOR/ENFORCE; BLOCK degrades to REDACT outside ENFORCE so values never leak. Adds tests and docs.

* feat(tealtiger): implement output scanning for tool results

Add functionality to scan tool outputs for PII and secrets before they
are returned to the agent's context. This includes support for
redacting sensitive information or blocking the entire result based
on configurable governance policies.

- Add `OutputAction` enum for REDACT, BLOCK, and FLAG actions
- Implement recursive string leaf scanning for structured tool results
- Add `output_scan` governance policy to `GovernancePolicy`

* fix(tealtiger): scan error results + reject empty output_scan PII categories

Addresses review on #3240.

1. Error results were skipped by output_scan. A tool that raises with an SSN

fix(mcp): decode resource template URI variables (#3250)

* fix(mcp): decode resource template URI variables

Decode matched URI variables once before invoking resource template readers,
preserving literal plus signs and the original URI in the read result.

Add file-backed regressions through both MCP protocol clients and document
the decoded-value contract for readers.

* fix(mcp): decode resource template URI variables safely

Implement secure percent-decoding for variables in `ResourceTemplate`.
The decoding process now ensures that plain variables (e.g., `{var}`)
cannot match URIs that, when decoded, would introduce path separators
(`/`) or escape the intended segment. This prevents "widening" the
match. Reserved variables (e.g., `{+var}`) are still permitted to
span multiple segments. Additionally, URIs with invalid UTF-8
sequences will now fail to match rather than decoding to replacement
characters.

- Update `_compile_template` to track segment-confined variables.
- Add `_decoded_variables` to handle strict UTF-8 decoding and
  segment validation.
- Update documentation to reflect the new decoding and matching rules.
- Add tests for encoded separators, path traversal attempts, and
  invalid UTF-8 sequences.

* refactor(mcp): swap the float-subclass idle-timeout sentinel for _MISSING

`_UntouchedIdleTimeout(float)` encoded "nobody supplied one" as a subclass of
the value itself, so the provenance rode along inside the number: it leaked
into the session manager, and any arithmetic would silently strip it. Nothing
else in `ag2/` subclasses a primitive to carry provenance.

Use the repo's existing idiom instead — `_MISSING = object()`, as in
`ag2/events/base.py` — resolved once in `__post_init__`. The field reads back
as the plain 1800.0 default, so the sentinel never reaches the SDK, and the
provenance lives in a public `asks_to_reap`.

That also removes `_reaping_was_asked_for`, a module-private helper `server.py`
was importing across a module boundary; the guard now reads
`transport.asks_to_reap`.

* feat(mcp): derive DNS rebinding protection, re-export its SDK types, drop the idle-timeout sentinel

Three follow-ups from review.

`security_settings` left alone no longer means "no protection". When an
authorization requirement is configured, `security.resource_url` is the
endpoint the operator declared this server answers on — not a guess about the
topology — so `allowed_hosts` and `allowed_origins` are derived from it, with
any port allowed when the URL names none. Opting out is now something you say:
`TransportSecuritySettings(enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False)`. With no
`security=` there is nothing to derive from and the protection stays off, as
before.

`TransportSecuritySettings` and `EventStore` join the curated SDK re-exports in
`ag2.mcp`. They are the two SDK types `TransportConfig` takes, and the
precedent the design cites — `RequestStateSecurity` — was already re-exported,
so reaching into `mcp.server.transport_security` for one of them was an
inconsistency.

`asks_to_reap` becomes a computed property and the `_MISSING` sentinel goes.
Storing it as a field leaked it into `asdict()` and inverted it under
`dataclasses.replace()`. The provenance distinction it protected is dropped
with it: spelling out the default number now reads the same as leaving the
field alone, which costs one diagnostic on `stateless=True` and removes the
machinery that diagnosis needed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(hitl): wait for the thread instead of racing the scheduler for it

`test_a_sync_sibling_is_still_never_owed_a_result` failed once on ubuntu 3.13
while every other job in the same run passed it. Not a flake in the usual sense
— the test asserted the converse of what the code guarantees, and the OS
scheduler decided which one it got.

A sync tool reaches its thread through `anyio.to_thread.run_sync`, which only
queues the work; `WorkerThread.run` then skips it outright when the future is
already cancelled. The sibling `ask_human` fails immediately with no HITL hook,
`ToolExecutor.execute_tools` cancels the batch with a raw `task.cancel()`, and
whether `slow_side_effect` runs at all comes down to whether the worker thread
woke before that cancel landed — locally about a millisecond of slack, which a
loaded CI container does not have.

Skipping the function is the better outcome, and the executor says so: it
guarantees no tool is left owed a result, not that every side effect was
stopped. So the test now waits on the seam it is actually about. `started` holds
the failure back until the sibling is demonstrably inside its thread, and `done`
replaces a hoped-for 0.4s sleep with the thread's own signal.

Reproduced deterministically by injecting 5ms of worker wake latency: the
original fails exactly as CI did, this passes. Load alone did not reproduce it
on a developer machine — 55 runs, none red — which is why the fix is a real
signal rather than a longer sleep.

feat(tealtiger): add rate_limit governance policy (#3246)

* feat(tealtiger): add rate_limit governance policy

Adds GovernancePolicy.rate_limit(max_calls, window_seconds, tool=None) — a
sliding-window cap on tool-call frequency. Where cost_limit caps cumulative
spend, this caps how fast calls happen, the defence against a runaway agent
loop that burns budget/rate-limits/side-effects before a cost ceiling notices.

- Global (tool=None) shares one budget across all tool calls; per-tool
  (tool=name or fnmatch pattern) scopes the limit to matching calls. Several
  compose; the first limit exceeded denies with RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (risk 70).
- Sliding window in seconds: only calls in the last window_seconds count.
  Timestamps live on the factory (shared across turns, cleared by reset()).
  Only allowed calls are counted, so a call denied by another policy never
  consumes the budget. OBSERVE skips; MONITOR records but does not block;
  ENFORCE blocks.
- Validation at construction: max_calls positive int, window_seconds positive
  number, tool non-empty if given.

test/extensions/tealtiger/test_rate_limit.py — 15 tests (global cap, per-tool
isolation, pattern family, global+per-tool compose, window expiry, mode
behavior, validation, end-to-end agent deny). Full extension suite: 198 passed
(was 183), ruff check + format clean. Docs: new Rate Limiting section, reason
code, summary-table row. No breaking changes — opt-in policy.

* fix(tealtiger): record a rate-limited call once per distinct bucket

Addresses review on #3246. _record_rate_limit_calls appended a timestamp
per matching policy, but several policies can share one bucket key (two
global limits both key '*', or two policies with the same tool pattern).
The bucket — not the policy — is what a window counts, so a single real call
was double-counted into a shared bucket: rate_limit(10, 60) + rate_limit(100,
3600) tripped the 10/min limit after ~5 real calls.

Fix: collect the distinct bucket keys the call matches and append exactly one
timestamp per key.

Regression tests: two global limits with different windows (5 calls -> 5
timestamps in '*', 10/min not tripped until the real 11th call), and two
policies sharing a tool pattern. Full extension suite: 200 passed, ruff
check + format clean.

* fix(tealtiger): key rate-limit history per policy, not per tool scope

Addresses review on #3246 (discussion r3992565377).

Policies that share a tool scope but use different windows were sharing
one timestamp list keyed by that scope. `_rate_limit_exceeded` pruned the
shared list to its own (short) window and wrote it back, so a
`rate_limit(10, 60)` policy running alongside `rate_limit(100, 3600)`
would delete every timestamp older than 60s before the hourly policy
could count them: the hour limit silently forgot prior calls, and the
outcome depended on policy order.

Key `_call_history` by policy index instead, so every rate_limit policy
owns its own list and prunes/counts only against its own window. A short
window can no longer evict entries a longer window still needs, and the
result is independent of declaration order. This also removes the need
for the earlier per-call dedup: each policy records the call once to its
own list, so two policies sharing a scope no longer double-count.

- middleware.py: `_call_history` is now `dict[int, list[float]]`; the
  `_evaluate` loop enumerates policies and passes the index to
  `_rate_limit_exceeded`; `_record_rate_limit_calls` appends to each
  matching policy's own list; `_rate_limit_key` removed. `reset()`
  still clears the history.
- test_rate_limit.py: existing state-peeking tests updated to the
  per-policy keys; the shared-bucket regression class reframed as
  per-policy counting; new `TestMixedWindowSharedScopePruning` ages
  calls out of the short window but inside the long one and asserts the
  long window still counts them and the short one refills, in both
  policy orders.

Full extension suite: 203 passed. ruff check + format clean.

* feat(tealtiger): enhance rate limiting with throttling and configurable actions

Improve the rate limiting mechanism in TealTiger to support both
throttling (waiting) and immediate refusal, providing better control
over runaway agent loops.

- Add `on_exceeded` parameter to `rate_limit` policy to choose between
  `"wait"` (default) and `"deny"`.
- Add `max_wait_seconds` to bound the duration a call can be held
  during throttling.
- Implement asynchronous waiting in `TealTigerMiddleware` when in
  `ENFORCE` mode.
- Update rate limit recording logic to ensure `MONITOR` mode does not
  consume window budget and `OBSERVE` mode does not fill windows.
- Switch to `time.monotonic()` for rate limit window calculations to
  ensure immunity to wall-clock changes.
- Update documentation and tests to reflect new capabilities and
  behavioral changes.

feat(skills): render a MemorySkill body per read (#3254)

* feat(skills): render a MemorySkill body per read

`SkillRuntime.read` was the one IO method left sync and context-free after
0005/0006, so a MemorySkill's `instructions` had to be a string frozen at
construction while its resources and scripts were already live callables.

Bring `read` in line with `read_resource` and `execute` — `async def read(name,
context)` — and let `instructions` be a callable. A callable body is wrapped
with `tool()` and rendered on every `load_skill` through the same
FastDepends-validated path as a resource, so it can use `Context` / `Variable` /
`Inject` dependency injection. `LocalRuntime.read` accepts and ignores the
context, as it already does for `read_resource`.

Only the body is dynamic: a skill's catalog entry stays the construction-time
snapshot that keeps it in lockstep with the activation tools' name enum.

fix(a2a): require only the chosen transport's SDK extra (#3257)

`a2a-sdk` ships the HTTP server and gRPC behind separate extras, but
`server.py` and `transports/_http.py` imported `transports.grpc` directly,
past the guard in `transports/__init__.py`. One missing `grpcio` therefore
broke the import of every A2A entry point, and the surviving guard could
only report the single extra hardcoded in its `except` — telling users to
install `a2a-sdk[http-server]` they already had, or `ag2[a2a]` in the case
of `build_card` and `A2AConfig`.

Route all three builders through the guarded package, and split the
starlette-bound route helper out of `transports/_common.py` so the mirrored
case holds too: a gRPC-only server no longer drags `starlette`. `A2AServer`
now imports on a bare `a2a-sdk`; only the `build_*` method whose transport
dependency is absent raises, naming that transport's own extra.

The docs pointed at `ag2[a2a-grpc]`, an extra that has never existed; they
now name the SDK extras that are actually installed.

Verified in clean environments: with `a2a-sdk[http-server]` and no `grpcio`,
`build_jsonrpc`/`build_rest` serve the agent card and `build_grpc` raises
with the gRPC hint; with `a2a-sdk[grpc]` and no starlette, the reverse.
`test/a2a/test_optional_dependencies.py` asserts the seam from the sources,
so it holds in the full development environment.

fix(subagents): lock max_concurrency semaphore provisioning per loop (#3243)

* fix(subagents): lock max_concurrency semaphore provisioning per loop

_spawn_subtask's check-then-act on self._task_slots races across OS
threads: two threads can both see no semaphore yet, each build their
own, and whichever assignment lands last silently discards the other,
so max_concurrency stops being enforced on the loop that lost.

Provision one Semaphore per running loop in a weakly-keyed map guarded
by a threading.Lock, so concurrent threads never clobber each other's
entry and a short-lived loop's entry is reclaimed once that loop is
gone.

Fixes #3242

* fix(agent): synchronize subtask slot creation per loop

Provision subtask concurrency semaphores through `_task_slots_for` under
a threading lock so concurrent OS threads driving the same Agent cannot
race while initializing task slots.

Drop closed loop entries while creating slots because contended asyncio
semaphores can cache their loop and keep weak keys alive. Update tests to
cover concurrent threads and loop cleanup.

fix(anthropic): report thinking tokens, and keep a measured zero a zero (#3259)

* fix(anthropic): report thinking tokens, and keep a measured zero a zero

`normalize_usage` read four keys off Anthropic's usage object and dropped the
rest, so `Usage.thinking_tokens` was always absent on Anthropic while the OpenAI
mapper filled it from `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`. Every
consumer inherited the hole — the AG-UI usage mapping, `UsageReport`, the eval
layer and the budget guard all saw a provider that appears never to reason.

Read `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`. It counts output tokens spent on
internal reasoning, so it is a decomposition of `output_tokens` rather than an
addition to it — the same rule the OpenAI mapper already follows, and no
consumer needs to learn a second one.

The cache counts had a second defect: written `float(cc) if cc else None`, a
count the provider measured as zero was recorded as a count never taken. ADR
0017 settles that distinction — `0` is a measurement, absence is the lack of
one — so the guard now tests presence. A live probe shows this is not an edge
case: every response carries `cache_creation_input_tokens: 0` and
`cache_read_input_tokens: 0` on a call that used no caching, so before this
change every Anthropic call reported both as never measured.

`server_tool_use`, `service_tier`, `inference_geo` and `cache_creation`'s
per-lifetime breakdown stay unmapped, with the reason stated on the mapper:
`Usage` carries whole-call token counts, and folding a request count or a
routing label into one is the derivation ADR 0017 forbids.

* docs(anthropic): clarify zero and absent usage counts

Tracing information, so it does not participate in equality, the same way

fix(events): stop Field.__get__ from retargeting shared descriptors (#3285)

A class-level read of an event field recorded its owner on the one
descriptor that parent and child event classes share, so any read of the
same field between `Event.field` and its comparison rebuilt the condition
for the wrong class. With threads interleaving, `ToolResultEvent.parent_id
== call.id` could come out as a `ToolErrorEvent` condition, and the tool
call then waited forever for a result it could no longer match. That is
the intermittent hang in
test_max_concurrency_holds_per_loop_under_concurrent_threads on Windows CI.

A class-level read now returns a copy bound to its owner, and a read
through an instance leaves the descriptor alone.

fix(context): strip reserved variables on every wire-originated sync (#3286)

`ConversationContext.variables` carries both user data and the framework's
own control-plane state: the `approval_required` allow-always bypass
(`ag:approval_required:always`), the A2A context-id bookkeeping and the
`a2a:tenant` override. Four transports sync that dict with a remote peer,
so a caller able to write a reserved key pre-approves a gated tool and the
human is never asked.

Moves the reserved-prefix filter into `ag2.context` as
`strip_reserved_variables` and applies it on both legs of all four
transports (a2a, a2ui, ag_ui, nlip), rather than leaving each transport to
decide for itself. Inbound merges warn on what they drop; outbound payloads
strip quietly, since the peer has no business reading this side's
control-plane state either.

Reported by @AUTHENSOR in #3255; refs #3256.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge commit from fork

* fix(tools): contain find_files glob matches within base_dir

FilesystemToolkit.find_files contained the `path` argument via _resolve_path
(is_relative_to) but passed `pattern` straight to Path.glob(). Path.relative_to
is purely lexical, so a pattern such as `../**/*` walked the parent of base_dir
and returned the names of files outside the configured root (read_only toolkits
were affected too). Contents stayed protected (read_file is contained), but
names and directory layout leaked.

Filter every match through resolve().is_relative_to(base_dir), mirroring the
containment read_file already applies; this also blocks symlinks inside base_dir
that point outside it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(tools): reject find_files patterns that escape base_dir before globbing

Filtering matches after Path.glob still walked outside base_dir, so a
pattern like '../../../../**/*' cost attacker-controlled I/O and leaked
directory existence through timing. Reject anchored patterns and '..'
segments up front, mirroring _resolve_path for `path`; keep the resolve()
filter for symlinks inside the base that point outside it.

feat(ag-ui): ask the human a question mid-run, and be answered (#3248)

* feat(ag-ui): ask the human a question mid-run, and be answered (#3202)

An AG-UI agent can now stop mid-run and ask. A tool calling
`context.input(...)` leaves the question as the outcome of the run that raised
it; the turn is held in the server, suspended exactly where it stopped, until a
later run on the same thread answers it through `resume`. The call resumes from
the line it stopped on, with its locals intact — nothing is replayed, because
the frame never died.

Tool-call approval rides the same path: an interrupt with
`reason="tool_approval"` carrying the `toolCallId`, answerable with a bare bool.

Both AG-UI transports serve this through one `serve_exchange`, so a client
cannot tell them apart, and a GET on the AG-UI route returns the capabilities
document.

Changes a default: a run with no human-input hook used to fail with "nobody
could be asked" and now pauses and asks the client. A supplied hook behaves
exactly as before. Held turns are bounded by `Retention(ttl=900, max_held=128)`,
the advertised `expiresAt` is the earlier of that bound and any
`context.input(timeout=)`, a resume is refused unless it echoes the proof issued
with its interrupt, and every refusal is a `RUN_ERROR` with a machine-readable
code rather than a stream that simply stops.

Requires `ag-ui-protocol>=0.1.21`, the first release whose resume entries carry
the metadata envelope the proof travels in.

One question is outstanding per turn: concurrent asking — parallel subtasks that
each ask a human — is refused with `HumanInputError` rather than silently
orphaning the first question. Serving several at once is follow-up work.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(ag-ui): improve interrupt test suite and type safety

Refactor the human-in-the-loop test suite to improve maintainability,
type coverage, and reliability.

- Flatten nested test classes in `test_interrupts.py` for better readability.
- Add explicit type annotations to test helpers in `test_refusals.py` and
  `test_resume_proof.py` to improve static analysis.
- Replace `asyncio.timeout` blocks with `asyncio.wait_for` in
  `test_turn_lifetime.py` to ensure consistent behavior during long-running
  test waits.
- Update `CODEOWNERS` to include `@vvlrff` for MCP-related files.

* fix(ag-ui): refuse a malformed resume proof instead of crashing the run

A proof arriving from a client went straight into `secrets.compare_digest`,
which raises `TypeError` rather than returning `False` when handed a non-ASCII
`str`. `serve_exchange` catches only `ResumeRefusedError`, so the generator died
after `RUN_STARTED` and left the client with no terminating event — and since
the turn had already been taken from the registry, it was then unreachable by
resume, sweep and eviction alike, held until the process went down. Proofs are
now compared as bytes, a turn taken for a resume is put back on any failure and
not only on a refusal, and a run already started on the wire is always
terminated on the wire.

Two smaller ones alongside it. `ServedTurns.release_all` was `async` but awaited
nothing, so shutdown scheduled its cancellations and returned before any held
turn had unwound; it now gathers and waits. And the guard against two questions
on one turn raised into a turn whose own exchange had already ended, so the
refusal reached no client and no log either; it now reports at `error` before
raising.

Also in this pass, from reviewing the two commits before it:

- Revert the `CODEOWNERS` change made in a9f66a1: it is unrelated to #3202.
- Drop `ToolApprovalRequest.tool_name`, which nothing read, and the `""` default
  on `tool_call_id`, which made an approval naming no call constructible.
- Declare `aclose` on the `A2UITransport` protocol instead of duck-checking it
  with `getattr`; `RestTransport` implements it as a no-op.
- Replace the per-turn `_discarder` closure with a class, per AGENTS.md.
- Cut `interrupts.__all__` from 29 names to 19 and re-export the four refusal
  codes from `ag2.ag_ui`, so nothing reaches into a private module for them.
- Rewrite `ag2/ag_ui/` docstrings against the openai SDK's conventions: no
  `Raises:`/`Returns:`/`Attributes:` sections, fields documented beneath
  themselves, backticks rather than Sphinx roles, and rationale moved into
  comments beside the code. 419 lines of docstring become 218.

* docs(ag-ui): document tool call lifecycle during interrupts

Add a warning to the user guide explaining that paused tool calls
span multiple runs. Clarify that events are split across different
`runId`s and that clients must track open tool calls by `threadId` to
correctly associate `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` events with their corresponding
starts.

* feat(ag-ui): implement human input and tool call interrupts

Refactor the AG-UI interrupt system to use more descriptive reason
codes and improve the robustness of the served agent lifecycle. This
includes a major overhaul of the testing infrastructure to support

Replace the built-in `TimeoutError` with `asyncio.TimeoutError` in

fix(tools): reject tools that share a name within a turn

The model calls a tool by name and a ToolCallEvent reaches every tool
subscribed to that name, so two tools named alike both ran on one call,
and an approval decision (including a denial) on one did not bind the
other.

Resolve each turn's tool schemas through resolve_tool_schemas, which
raises ToolConflictError naming both sources when a function name is
exposed twice or equals a built-in tool's name. Agent and LiveAgent both
use it, after toolkits such as MCPToolkit discover their tools, so names
from every source (agent tools, ask(tools=...), toolkits, plugins,
sub-task, knowledge and deferred tools) are checked. Repeated built-in
schema types (several MCPServerTool servers) stay allowed.

Records the decision in ADR 0020 and documents it on the tools and MCP
pages.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(tools): resolve tools sharing a name by precedence

Replace the duplicate-name error with precedence, so a turn still
exposes one schema and registers one tool per name while overriding a
tool stays possible:

- tools declared in code override each other by order (later wins,
  debug log only); built-in tools count as declared in code;
- tools an MCP server reports rank below tools declared in code,
  wherever the toolkit sits, and are dropped with a warning;
- between MCP servers the first server's tool wins, the rest are
  dropped with a warning suggesting tool_name_prefix.

resolve_tools (ag2/tools/precedence.py) resolves toolkits member by
member after discovery and registers pruned copies, so a dropped tool
is never subscribed and never receives a call. Agent and LiveAgent use
it. ToolConflictError keeps its original signature.

ADR 0020 and the tools/MCP docs pages describe the precedence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(tools): key approval grants by tool implementation, rank client tools below code

The "always" answer of approval_required was keyed by tool name, so a grant
for one implementation approved another tool of the same name on a later
turn (e.g. a local deploy, then an MCP server's deploy), including through a
hook shared by both. A tool now stamps ToolCallEvent.source on its copy of
the call before its middleware runs (function module:qualname:name, or the
MCP endpoint and remote tool name), and the grant is keyed by it. The key is
deterministic, so it survives rebuilding the agent from stored variables.

ClientTool (tools a client sends over AG-UI, A2A or NLIP) now ranks below
tools declared in code, so a client can no longer replace a server tool of
the same name. Overriding a tool declared in code logs a warning instead of
a debug line, since the replaced tool may have carried an approval gate.

Tests for tool-name collisions now go through the public API only: a real
served MCPServer instead of patching _mcp_session, CascadeConfig instead of
a MagicMock live config, AG-UI RunAgentInput.tools for client tools.

fix(mcp): keep a conversation alive while any turn runs on it (#3311)

* fix(mcp): never evict a session store entry with a turn in flight

* fix(mcp): keep a conversation alive while any turn runs on it

Builds on the previous commit, which stopped idle expiry and LRU overflow
from dropping a conversation whose turn lock is held. Three gaps remained:

- Overflow counted the conversation being handed out as idle, since its
  turn lock is taken only after the registry returns it. With every other
  conversation mid-turn, a new caller was given a handle that was already
  evicted.
- `last` was refreshed only when a turn started, so a turn slower than the
  ttl survived but was expired by the very next request. The end of a turn
  now counts as use, refreshed synchronously so a cancelled turn cannot
  lose it.
- A resumed modern-era run continues without the turn lock it released
  when it paused, so it could still have its history dropped mid-run.

* fix(sandbox): block &, newline, CR and < in the restricted shell filter

In restricted mode (allowed=[...] or readonly=True) ShellAdapter checks
the head command against the allow-list and rejects shell operators, then
runs the whole string through `sh -c`. The operator list missed the `&`
and newline command separators, so e.g. "git status & touch x" or
"cat f\ntouch x" passed the filter and ran the second command
(GHSA-2h4w-29cv-2cmv). Also block `\r` and `<` (input redirect and bash
`<(...)` process substitution) as hardening.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sandbox): stop readonly commands from writing files or running commands

readonly=True only checked the head command, so an allowed entry could
still write or execute through its own arguments: `env touch x`,
`find . -exec ...`, `sort -o x`, `git diff --output=x`. Drop `env` and
reject those arguments on the parsed argv. Long options match by prefix,
since GNU tools accept abbreviations (`sort --outp=x`), and an argument
with `$` is refused because the shell expands it after the check
(`-e${EMPTY}xec`).
